articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

Editorial Context: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.
• Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Brace for impact: On rising inflation and external factors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: High inflation due to external factors could soon exacerbate economic pain

India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: Six arrested for running illegal LPG refilling unit in Hyderabad, 46 domestic cylinders seized
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hyderabad City Police arrested six persons for running an illegal LPG refilling unit at a scrap shop in Bapu Ghat, Langer Houz, and seized 46 domestic LPG cylinders, 36 small cylinders and refilling equipment worth approximately ₹4 lakh.

The Commissioner’s Task Force, Golconda Zone team, in a joint operation with Langer Houz police and the Assistant Civil Supplies Officer (ACSO), Mehdipatnam circle, raided the premises following credible information about the illegal activity.

According to the police, the accused were transferring LPG from domestic cylinders into smaller commercial cylinders of 3 kg and 5 kg capacity using refilling equipment, without taking necessary safety precautions. They were selling the refilled cylinders in the black market to customers to make illegal profits.

The police identified the arrested persons as Ravi (29), a resident of Langer Houz, Sohail (19) and Pankaj (20), both residents of Prashanth Nagar, Langer Houz, Vicky, a labourer and LPG cylinder supplier associated with an HP Gas agency, Ramu (32), an auto owner involved in supplying HP Gas cylinders from SK Agencies, Langer Houz and Raju (47), a labourer from Mangar Basti, Mallepally.

During the raid, the police seized 46 full domestic HP Gas cylinders, 35 empty 3 kg cylinders, one empty 5 kg cylinder, a weighing machine, seven gas-refilling kits and two trolley autos bearing registration numbers TG 13 T 1244 and TS 13 QA 9722. The total value of the seized property was estimated at ₹4 lakh.

articles.title: CJP leaders appear before SEM in Jantar Mantar tresspass case; Saurav Das’ Delhi address verified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Second appearance since their release from Tihar jail on October 21; Das says Delhi Police took a month to verify his address, while Ranka hopes the club concept spreads across the country.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Ritu Raj at Delhi’s Mandir Marg police station on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in connection with the Jantar Mantar trespassing case, with Mr. Das submitting documents to verify his residential address in the Capital.

The duo spent over three hours at the police station. Speaking to the media after the proceedings, Mr. Das said they had waited for about two hours for the Magistrate to arrive, after which the proceedings began.

“This hearing was basically for them to verify where in Delhi I live. It is a matter of fact that the Delhi Police is aware where I live, but for the last one month they haven’t been able to verify that. And they have a force of one lakh police officers. It’s surprising that one lakh officers are not able to verify where I live,” he said.
Mr. Das said he had now submitted the required documents and that his address had been verified. He added that the documents were submitted on the condition that they would not be leaked.
“The presiding Judge has given the order to ensure the documents don’t leak from either the court or the police’s side,” he said.
He also appealed to the media not to forward any documents pertaining to him if they received them, and instead share them with him so that the matter could be taken up in court.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das hit back at funding charges during CJP press meet

This was the duo’s second appearance before the SEM since their release from Tihar jail on October 21, following seven days in judicial custody. They had last appeared before the Magistrate on October 23, when Mr. Das was asked to furnish a verifiable document corroborating his present residential address in Delhi.

At the time of their release, the two had furnished personal and surety bonds and submitted written undertakings before the SEM that they would not call for any protest at Jantar Mantar as long as it remained a denotified protest site. They had also assured the court that they would not engage in any activity that could breach peace.
They were directed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.

articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) agreed to have a detailed hearing of an application filed by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders, who have posed 48 ‘interrogatories’ directly to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and senior poll officials regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The interrogatories challenge the veracity of “bare assertions” made by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in an institutional affidavit filed on October 26 . One of these assertions was that the decision to hold a nationwide SIR, which saw around 13 crore voters excluded from the electoral rolls, was “unanimous”.

The interrogatories intend to compel the two Election Commissioners to individually state on oath whether they had objected to the SIR orders. The interrogatories require the CEC, the Election Commissioners, and poll officials to support their every answer with documentary proof in court.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9 after senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the ECI, enquired if the court would have enough time to hear the multiple petitions in the post-lunch session.

Senior advocates Kapil Sibal, A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., for the INDIA bloc leaders, urged the Bench, which was about to rise for lunch after the morning session when Mr. Salve intervened, to issue notice on the application containing the interrogatories.

Though, initially, the court agreed to issue notice to the ECI for a response, Mr. Salve, along with senior advocate Maninder Singh, opposed the issuance of any notice before a preliminary hearing on the application.
“We will then hear the application and pass necessary orders,” the CJI said.

The application was filed as part of the Opposition leaders’ writ petition claiming the nationwide SIR exercise, the manner and extent of its conduct, was the product of a unilateral exercise of power by the CEC without the knowledge, approval or concurrence of the Election Commissioners.

Mr. Gandhi and the Opposition leaders submitted that posing the interrogatories was necessary as the controversy in their petition substantially rested upon facts that lie exclusively within the knowledge and the records of the ECI. The petitioners said they had no means of access to those facts except through the ECI and their officials.
So far, rather than disclosing those facts, the ECI has only made bare assertions.

articles.title: Congress manifesto remains unfulfilled even after 3 years of unveiling: Harish Rao
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Deputy Floor leader of the BRS Legislature Party and former minister T. Harish Rao has alleged that the Congress party’s ‘Abhaya Hastham’ manifesto has turned out to be an empty hand instead of the promise of being a hand of fulfilment, even three years after its announcement.

In a statement, Mr. Rao said on Tuesday (November 17) that the Congress party had unveiled and announced its manifesto for the Assembly elections in 2023 terming it to be a ‘Bhagavadgita’, Bible and Quran for the party and it would be implemented within a year of coming to power, come what may. However, after three years — it was on November 17 the manifesto was announced in 2023 — it remains unfulfilled.

The manifesto was announced by the then PCC president and present Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy in the presence of AICC leaders Sonia Gandhi and Mallikarjuna Kharge and manifesto committee chairman D. Sridhar Babu and present Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka, among others. It was also promised to provide constitutional guarantee to the six guarantees by making legislations in support of their implementation.

However, three years later and after holding 38 Cabinet meetings the six guarantees were not provided with the backing of legislation, the manifesto remains a book of empty promises. In the process, the ruling party had also deceived gods and religious books. He asked all those who were present at the unveiling of the manifesto to answer people as to why it was not implemented.

Meanwhile BRS leaders staged a protest at Telangana Bhavan by tearing up copies of the Congress party’s Abhaya Hastham manifesto and throwing them into a dustbin. They questioned the fate of promises made to the people of Telangana and demanded accountability from Rahul Gandhi and the Congress leadership.

Party leaders G. Jagadish Reddy, V. Srinivas Goud, Balka Suman, Methuku Anand, M. Yadagiri Reddy, N. Bhaskar Rao and others asked the Congress leaders to go through promises made in the manifesto and tell people how many of them were fulfilled in three years.

articles.title: Karnataka Lokayukta directs Bengaluru West City Corporation Commissioner to fix accountability for inaction on illegal construction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Karnataka Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner of the Bengaluru West City Corporation to identify officials responsible for failing to act against an unauthorised construction in Rajarajeshwari Nagar and initiate appropriate action against those found responsible.

The direction follows a complaint filed by K. Manjunath of Ramachandrapura, alleging that officials of the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), now part of the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s Bengaluru West City Corporation, failed to take action against illegal construction at Site No. 67 in Ward No. 160 of the Rajarajeshwarinagar Sub-Division.

According to the complaint, the property owner, N.S. Balachandra Dutta, had obtained building permission for a basement, ground floor and two upper floors. However, the owner allegedly proceeded to construct two additional floors in violation of the sanctioned plan and building bye-laws.

Despite the issuance of notices under Sections 248(1), 248(2) and 248(3) of the BBMP Act, 2020, followed by a confirmation order under Section 356(1) on September 3, 2024, the unauthorised construction was allegedly not removed.

The authority noted that no effective steps had been taken to execute the confirmation order. Despite repeated directions, reminders, and a show-cause notice, the Executive Engineer concerned also failed to submit an action-taken report.

Executive Engineer S.L. Papireddy, who appeared before the authority on Monday (November 16) in response to a summons, stated that the order issued under Section 356(1) had not been communicated to him.

Taking serious note of the continued inaction, the Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner to examine the matter, identify the officials responsible for the lapses, fix accountability and initiate appropriate action against the erring officials.
The Commissioner has been directed to appear in person before the authority on December 7 and submit a detailed report.

articles.title: A poverty line that falls short
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Reliable poverty estimates are not just for academic purposes. India has made real progress, but without a credible benchmark, it is hard to say how much, or how much remains to be done

There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.

India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.
Macroeconomic & Financial Update: A poverty line that falls short. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and banking sector resilience.

fullParagraphs: The government late Monday (November 16, 2026) hiked the export duty on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹2.5 per litre and ₹1.5 per litre, whilst keeping the levy on export of petrol unchanged at nil.
Duty rates on petrol and diesel meant for domestic consumption remain unchanged.
The hike in diesel levy assumes added significance as India looks to further up their exports of the vehicular fuel to Europe amid a global supply crunch.
In the upcoming fortnight, diesel exports would draw a levy of ₹14 per litre compared to ₹11.5 per litre mandated for the previous fortnight.
ATF exports would draw a levy of ₹12.5 per litre against ₹11 per litre.

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance

Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

articles.title: Equity vs bonds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Concentrated bets in equity market could generate high returns if your bet turns right; On the other hand, diversification pays off for bond investments

Diversification may have its virtues but so does concentrated investments. Sector funds are examples of concentrated bets. In this article, we draw a distinction between concentrated bets in the equity and the bond markets and show why the former is meaningful and the latter, somewhat risky.

In theory, equity has unlimited upside potential. That means stock prices can rise to any level. In the real world, stock prices have high, not unlimited, upside potential given our finite investment horizon. Yet, concentrated bets can be meaningful. If you expect the banking sector to do well in the coming year, buying units of a banking sector ETF or a sector fund could be optimal. But the downside can be high if your bet turns wrong.
Macroeconomic & Financial Update: Equity vs bonds. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and banking sector resilience.

Concentrated bets in equity market could generate high returns if your bet turns right; On the other hand, diversification pays off for bond investments

Diversification may have its virtues but so does concentrated investments. Sector funds are examples of concentrated bets. In this article, we draw a distinction between concentrated bets in the equity and the bond markets and show why the former is meaningful and the latter, somewhat risky.

In theory, equity has unlimited upside potential. That means stock prices can rise to any level. In the real world, stock prices have high, not unlimited, upside potential given our finite investment horizon. Yet, concentrated bets can be meaningful. If you expect the banking sector to do well in the coming year, buying units of a banking sector ETF or a sector fund could be optimal. But the downside can be high if your bet turns wrong.

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: Quad announces Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi

The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness”
“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.
In a joint press release following the Quad meeting in Manila, the group said that it “affirms the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.”
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” it added.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed ways to strengthen cooperation and exchanged views on regional and global developments with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand in separate bilateral meetings in the Philippines.

Mr. Modi, who arrived in Manila on Monday to attend the ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit, met Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on the sidelines of the two summits.
PM Modi, at the Quad meeting in Manila, announced that the inaugural Quad Business Leaders Forum will be hosted in Mumbai in 2027, the Ministry of External Affairs said.

The Ministry of External Affairs said that at the Quad meeting, PM Modi “reaffirmed India’s commitment to a constructive and reliable Quad partnership, advancing peace, prosperity and resilience in the Indo-Pacific through cooperation in maritime security, economic security, critical technologies and disaster response.”

U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed four key outcomes of the Quad leaders’ meeting in Manila, covering economic cooperation, artificial intelligence, maritime security and cybersecurity, as leaders of India, the United States, Japan and Australia gathered for the high-level engagement.
The four outcomes include the Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, Super Intelligence Accelerator, Maritime Intelligence Sharing Corporation and Quad cybersecurity intelligence-sharing cooperation.

articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.
Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.
India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

articles.title: Fresh unrest in Bangladesh as garment workers protest, block highways for higher wages
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways

Authorities in Bangladesh on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) deployed more than 1,000 paramilitary personnel as garment workers staged demonstrations and clashed with police in the industrial belt around Dhaka, demanding higher wages and blocking three major highways.

Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, disrupting traffic and causing long tailbacks.
The demonstrations are part of weeks of intermittent protests that began in late October across Bangladesh's major garment-producing areas.
The workers have been demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from the existing Tk 12,500 ($100) to Tk 30,000 ($240), citing rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare.

Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for more than 80% of the country's export earnings, with prolonged disruption threatening production schedules, international buyers' confidence and global apparel supply chains.
In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said it had deployed 42 platoons of personnel in the industrial hubs of Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj. Officials said the personnel were also using drones to maintain surveillance over readymade garment factory workers.

Police said two of the three highways had been cleared, but intermittent blockades continued to cause heavy traffic congestion on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway. "We are working to clear the highways and disperse the protesters," a police spokesperson said.

The industrial unrest also affected factory operations. Police said at least 37 garment factories across the industrial belt were declared closed on Tuesday, while dozens more temporarily suspended production after workers left their workplaces to join demonstrations.

In Dhaka, garment workers gathered in the Darus Salam and Shah Ali police station areas of Mirpur on Tuesday morning and attempted to move towards the Mirpur-10 roundabout, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.

Authorities in Bangladesh on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) deployed more than 1,000 paramilitary personnel as garment workers staged demonstrations and clashed with police in the industrial belt around Dhaka, demanding higher wages and blocking three major highways.

Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, disrupting traffic and causing long tailbacks.

The demonstrations are part of weeks of intermittent protests that began in late October across Bangladesh's major garment-producing areas.

The workers have been demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from the existing Tk 12,500 ($100) to Tk 30,000 ($240), citing rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare.

Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for more than 80% of the country's export earnings, with prolonged disruption threatening production schedules, international buyers' confidence and global apparel supply chains.

In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said it had deployed 42 platoons of personnel in the industrial hubs of Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj. Officials said the personnel were also using drones to maintain surveillance over readymade garment factory workers.

Police said two of the three highways had been cleared, but intermittent blockades continued to cause heavy traffic congestion on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway. "We are working to clear the highways and disperse the protesters," a police spokesperson said.

The industrial unrest also affected factory operations. Police said at least 37 garment factories across the industrial belt were declared closed on Tuesday, while dozens more temporarily suspended production after workers left their workplaces to join demonstrations.

In Dhaka, garment workers gathered in the Darus Salam and Shah Ali police station areas of Mirpur on Tuesday morning and attempted to move towards the Mirpur-10 roundabout, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.

articles.title: Burnham delays tabling of options for U.K.-EU ties
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has delayed unveiling options for long-term ties between the U.K.- and EU The Prime Minister had said in September that he would set out options — including the option of a complete return to the EU — around the U.K.-EU Summit, which is scheduled for Friday.

“This will take time and we will present those options and our assessment of them to inform decisions in the next Parliament,” Mr. Burnham said on Monday at the annual City Hall banquet in the capital’s financial hub.
“At every stage, the British people will be the boss,” he added.

At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer. Mr. Burnham suggested this deal could increase the U.K.’s GDP by 0.4%.

Legislation for the deal will be presented to the U.K. Parliament next week, the Prime Minister said, as he ruled out crossing red lines, i.e., ruling out joining the EU, allowing the “free movement” of EU citizens across the border or taking the U.K. into the EU Customs Union and Single Market during this Parliament (which ends in 2029).

EU Affairs Minister Hamish Falconer said that a U.K.-EU agreement would involve an “exit clause” in case a future U.K. government run by the Conservatives or Reform U.K. undid the deal, the BBC reported. These two opposition parties have said they would undo any agreement reached by Labour. The exit clause it is likely to involve payments to Brussels to set up border infrastructure.
During his speech Mr. Burnham also spoke of reviving the Commonwealth (of which India is also a part) group of nations.
“It is a unique geopolitical forum, not including either the US or China, and yet we have failed to invest energy in modernising the Commonwealth,” he said.
The Prime Minister said Britain would offer countries a structured dialogue in 2027 on its historical role in slavery but would not make financial reparations for it.

“It is basic good manners, if a friend wants to talk about something that is unjust and unresolved, to listen and engage,” he said. Longstanding calls from Caribbean nations for reparations and apologies grew louder in recent weeks, around a visit of King Charles III to the region.

articles.title: Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, eight people arrested
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from

Eight people were detained in central Assam’s Hojai district after they clashed with Forest Department personnel on Monday night (November 16, 2026) during an operation to guide a female elephant back to the jungle it came from.

The Forest officials fired “sera bullets” (pellets) from a pump-action gun to divert the elephant away from a human settlement. Five people were injured in the firing, triggering the mob violence and leaving two personnel injured.
Forest officials claimed three people sustained pellet injuries. The injured, including one of the two personnel, were admitted to a local hospital for treatment.

Divisional Forest Officer Nayan Jyoti Rajbongshi said a herd of elephants from the hills of Karbi Anglong entered the Hawaipur Reserve Forest in Hojai on Monday morning. Barring the female elephant, estimated to be 40 years old, the herd returned to Karbi Anglong a few hours later.
“We received information about the movement of the female elephant, possibly separated from the herd, along a road in a revenue area. We managed to push it into the Hawaipur Reserve Forest,” he said.
However, the elephant emerged from the forest around dusk and headed toward a village. The Forest personnel fired the pellets to drive it away, but some villagers were injured in the process.
“The police brought the situation under control and picked up eight people who clashed with our personnel. The police recorded the statement of our personnel,” Mr. Rajbongshi said.
Wildlife officials said people often obstruct rescue operations by gathering around a wild animal that strays out of a forest.
According to Assam government data tabled in the 126-member Assembly in July, as many as 1,147 people and 246 elephants were killed in human-elephant conflicts in the State since 2016.

Mr. Modi had used the “Abki baar, 400-paar” slogan during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, seeking a mandate of more than 400 seats for the National Democratic Alliance.

Several air quality monitoring stations in Delhi have recorded AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category (400-500) over the past few days. The city’s average AQI had also crossed the 400-mark on Friday (November 13, 2026).

articles.title: Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space companies to develop High-Resolution Indian Human Settlement Layers (IHSL) across Indian cities.

The three companies, SpacePixxel Technologies Pvt. Ltd. , KaleidEO Space Systems Pvt. Ltd. and Azista Industries Pvt. Ltd. have been selected under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme for Use Case Demonstration by Non-Government Entities (NGEi) to develop IHSL across Indian cities.

These companies will collectively receive seed funding of ₹1.46 crore to develop and demonstrate an indigenous satellite-based system for 3D reconstruction of India’s built environment using monocular imageries.

IN-SPACe said that the initiative, undertaken under the Announcement of Opportunity (AO) for the development of high-resolution IHSL, aims to address the NITI Aayog’s requirement of having an accurate and detailed geospatial data on human settlement which can be used for urban planning, infrastructure development and disaster risk assessment in addition to population assessment.

The selected companies will develop models using Earth Observation data to generate three integrated outputs covering built-up surface and building type, building height, and built-up volume. The deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.
The techniques will be developed at a high spatial resolution using Indian satellite data.

The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, representing distinct urban contexts of a large metropolitan region and a hill city. The pilot project will derive settlement patterns across two time periods, enabling comparisons of urban growth and changes in built-up density over time.

“India’s cities are expanding rapidly, both horizontally and vertically. Effective urban planning requires an accurate understanding of the built environment, but critical data gaps often limit this. This initiative addresses that gap by bringing together Indian satellite data, indigenous technology and clearly defined requirements from government departments. It gives Indian companies an opportunity to develop solutions for real-world urban challenges. More importantly, successful pilots can lay the foundation for scalable, homegrown capabilities that can be deployed across Indian cities,” Dr. Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe, said.

“Starting with Bengaluru and Shimla, this IN-SPACe supported project will provide pathways to build indigenous satellite data on human settlements, allowing recognition of urbanisation as it happens.” said Shamika Ravi, Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)
Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 17 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space companies to develop High-Resolution Indian Human Settlement Layers (IHSL) across Indian cities.

The three companies, SpacePixxel Technologies Pvt. Ltd. , KaleidEO Space Systems Pvt. Ltd. and Azista Industries Pvt. Ltd. have been selected under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme for Use Case Demonstration by Non-Government Entities (NGEi) to develop IHSL across Indian cities.

These companies will collectively receive seed funding of ₹1.46 crore to develop and demonstrate an indigenous satellite-based system for 3D reconstruction of India’s built environment using monocular imageries.

IN-SPACe said that the initiative, undertaken under the Announcement of Opportunity (AO) for the development of high-resolution IHSL, aims to address the NITI Aayog’s requirement of having an accurate and detailed geospatial data on human settlement which can be used for urban planning, infrastructure development and disaster risk assessment in addition to population assessment.

The selected companies will develop models using Earth Observation data to generate three integrated outputs covering built-up surface and building type, building height, and built-up volume. The deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

The techniques will be developed at a high spatial resolution using Indian satellite data.

The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, representing distinct urban contexts of a large metropolitan region and a hill city. The pilot project will derive settlement patterns across two time periods, enabling comparisons of urban growth and changes in built-up density over time.

“India’s cities are expanding rapidly, both horizontally and vertically. Effective urban planning requires an accurate understanding of the built environment, but critical data gaps often limit this. This initiative addresses that gap by bringing together Indian satellite data, indigenous technology and clearly defined requirements from government departments. It gives Indian companies an opportunity to develop solutions for real-world urban challenges. More importantly, successful pilots can lay the foundation for scalable, homegrown capabilities that can be deployed across Indian cities,” Dr. Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe, said.

“Starting with Bengaluru and Shimla, this IN-SPACe supported project will provide pathways to build indigenous satellite data on human settlements, allowing recognition of urbanisation as it happens.” said Shamika Ravi, Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)

Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received.

articles.title: Nvidia to reveal first earnings since spy scandal
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis
AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit and the United States to tighten export curbs on chips.
Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

Mr. Huang, perhaps the tech industry's most recognised booster of AI, stepped down on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The scandal has battered shares of Nvidia -- until recently the world's most valuable publicly traded company -- which is at the centre of an AI buildout that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe.

Washington announced new restrictions on Monday (November 16) on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing just before the high-profile APEC summit where U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are set for talks.
Beijing's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests".

The new U.S. export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi's talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, which starts Wednesday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington's new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a U.S. license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under U.S. arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil -- countries the U.S. commerce department says present a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on U.S. hardware not available for export to China.

articles.title: In line with WHO framework, T.N.’s National Centre of Ageing provides integrated care for the elderly
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: WHO’s approach is to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care

Maintaining physical and mental capacities is key to ensuring that older persons remain functionally independent. With age-related conditions such as visual and hearing impairment, memory and mobility issues often remaining undetected or unaddressed in the elderly, the National Centre of Ageing (NCA), Guindy has started to focus on providing integrated care to help older persons maintain functional ability. This is in line with the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) integrated care for older people approach (ICOPE).

According to the WHO, numerous physiological changes occur, and the risks of experiencing a decline in physical and mental capacities (intrinsic capacity) and having more than one condition (disease) increase when people age. This could manifest as cognitive decline, limited mobility, hearing loss, malnutrition, vision impairment, depressive symptoms, urinary incontinence and falls. ICOPE is WHO’s approach to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care. It supports optimising intrinsic capacity and functional ability in older age, it said.

Science, Space & Environment Report: In line with WHO framework, T.N.’s National Centre of Ageing provides integrated care for the elderly. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.summary: WHO’s approach is to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care
articles.keyPoints:
• WHO’s approach is to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care
• Maintaining physical and mental capacities is key to ensuring that older persons remain functionally independent. With age-related conditions such as visual and hearing impairment, memory and mobility issues often remaining undetected or unaddressed in the elderly, the National Centre of Ageing (NCA), Guindy has started to focus on providing integrated care to help older persons maintain functional ability. This is in line with the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) integrated care for older people approach (ICOPE).
• According to the WHO, numerous physiological changes occur, and the risks of experiencing a decline in physical and mental capacities (intrinsic capacity) and having more than one condition (disease) increase when people age. This could manifest as cognitive decline, limited mobility, hearing loss, malnutrition, vision impairment, depressive symptoms, urinary incontinence and falls. ICOPE is WHO’s approach to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care. It supports optimising intrinsic capacity and functional ability in older age, it said.

fullParagraphs: High inflation due to external factors could soon exacerbate economic pain

India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.
