articles.title: Six arrested for running illegal LPG refilling unit in Hyderabad, 46 domestic cylinders seized
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hyderabad City Police arrested six persons for running an illegal LPG refilling unit at a scrap shop in Bapu Ghat, Langer Houz, and seized 46 domestic LPG cylinders, 36 small cylinders and refilling equipment worth approximately ₹4 lakh.

The Commissioner’s Task Force, Golconda Zone team, in a joint operation with Langer Houz police and the Assistant Civil Supplies Officer (ACSO), Mehdipatnam circle, raided the premises following credible information about the illegal activity.

According to the police, the accused were transferring LPG from domestic cylinders into smaller commercial cylinders of 3 kg and 5 kg capacity using refilling equipment, without taking necessary safety precautions. They were selling the refilled cylinders in the black market to customers to make illegal profits.

The police identified the arrested persons as Ravi (29), a resident of Langer Houz, Sohail (19) and Pankaj (20), both residents of Prashanth Nagar, Langer Houz, Vicky, a labourer and LPG cylinder supplier associated with an HP Gas agency, Ramu (32), an auto owner involved in supplying HP Gas cylinders from SK Agencies, Langer Houz and Raju (47), a labourer from Mangar Basti, Mallepally.

During the raid, the police seized 46 full domestic HP Gas cylinders, 35 empty 3 kg cylinders, one empty 5 kg cylinder, a weighing machine, seven gas-refilling kits and two trolley autos bearing registration numbers TG 13 T 1244 and TS 13 QA 9722. The total value of the seized property was estimated at ₹4 lakh.

articles.title: CJP leaders appear before SEM in Jantar Mantar tresspass case; Saurav Das’ Delhi address verified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Second appearance since their release from Tihar jail on October 21; Das says Delhi Police took a month to verify his address, while Ranka hopes the club concept spreads across the country.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Ritu Raj at Delhi’s Mandir Marg police station on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in connection with the Jantar Mantar trespassing case, with Mr. Das submitting documents to verify his residential address in the Capital.

The duo spent over three hours at the police station. Speaking to the media after the proceedings, Mr. Das said they had waited for about two hours for the Magistrate to arrive, after which the proceedings began.

“This hearing was basically for them to verify where in Delhi I live. It is a matter of fact that the Delhi Police is aware where I live, but for the last one month they haven’t been able to verify that. And they have a force of one lakh police officers. It’s surprising that one lakh officers are not able to verify where I live,” he said.
Mr. Das said he had now submitted the required documents and that his address had been verified. He added that the documents were submitted on the condition that they would not be leaked.
“The presiding Judge has given the order to ensure the documents don’t leak from either the court or the police’s side,” he said.
He also appealed to the media not to forward any documents pertaining to him if they received them, and instead share them with him so that the matter could be taken up in court.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das hit back at funding charges during CJP press meet

This was the duo’s second appearance before the SEM since their release from Tihar jail on October 21, following seven days in judicial custody. They had last appeared before the Magistrate on October 23, when Mr. Das was asked to furnish a verifiable document corroborating his present residential address in Delhi.

At the time of their release, the two had furnished personal and surety bonds and submitted written undertakings before the SEM that they would not call for any protest at Jantar Mantar as long as it remained a denotified protest site. They had also assured the court that they would not engage in any activity that could breach peace.
They were directed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.

articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) agreed to have a detailed hearing of an application filed by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders, who have posed 48 ‘interrogatories’ directly to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and senior poll officials regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The interrogatories challenge the veracity of “bare assertions” made by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in an institutional affidavit filed on October 26 . One of these assertions was that the decision to hold a nationwide SIR, which saw around 13 crore voters excluded from the electoral rolls, was “unanimous”.

The interrogatories intend to compel the two Election Commissioners to individually state on oath whether they had objected to the SIR orders. The interrogatories require the CEC, the Election Commissioners, and poll officials to support their every answer with documentary proof in court.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9 after senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the ECI, enquired if the court would have enough time to hear the multiple petitions in the post-lunch session.

Senior advocates Kapil Sibal, A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., for the INDIA bloc leaders, urged the Bench, which was about to rise for lunch after the morning session when Mr. Salve intervened, to issue notice on the application containing the interrogatories.

Though, initially, the court agreed to issue notice to the ECI for a response, Mr. Salve, along with senior advocate Maninder Singh, opposed the issuance of any notice before a preliminary hearing on the application.
“We will then hear the application and pass necessary orders,” the CJI said.

The application was filed as part of the Opposition leaders’ writ petition claiming the nationwide SIR exercise, the manner and extent of its conduct, was the product of a unilateral exercise of power by the CEC without the knowledge, approval or concurrence of the Election Commissioners.

Mr. Gandhi and the Opposition leaders submitted that posing the interrogatories was necessary as the controversy in their petition substantially rested upon facts that lie exclusively within the knowledge and the records of the ECI. The petitioners said they had no means of access to those facts except through the ECI and their officials.
So far, rather than disclosing those facts, the ECI has only made bare assertions.

articles.title: 10-day Nilgiris Book Festival to begin on November 27
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Nilgiris district administration has announced that the 5th Nilgiris Book Festival-2026 will be held from November 27 to December 6.

In a press release, the district administration said the book festival was part of the initiatives being undertaken by the State government to promote the habit of reading among school students and the general public. The festival is to be organised jointly by the Nilgiris district administration, the Public Libraries Department and the Booksellers and Publishers Association of South India (BAPASI) and will be held at the Resource Centre for Tribal Development on Garden Road in Udhagamandalam.

The book festival will take place over a period of 10 days and will be open to visitors from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. “More than 50 publishers, who are members of BAPASI, will participate in the festival and display their books for sale. Renowned speakers from across Tamil Nadu, along with writers from the Nilgiris district, will also participate in the event,” a press release added.

Various programmes, including book-related events, will be organised as part of the festival. These will include activities aimed at showcasing the talents of school and college students from the district, as well as cultural programmes, art performances and other literary activities, it was stated.
District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru requested members of the public, school and college students, and teachers to attend the festival.

articles.title: Karnataka Lokayukta directs Bengaluru West City Corporation Commissioner to fix accountability for inaction on illegal construction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Karnataka Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner of the Bengaluru West City Corporation to identify officials responsible for failing to act against an unauthorised construction in Rajarajeshwari Nagar and initiate appropriate action against those found responsible.

The direction follows a complaint filed by K. Manjunath of Ramachandrapura, alleging that officials of the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), now part of the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s Bengaluru West City Corporation, failed to take action against illegal construction at Site No. 67 in Ward No. 160 of the Rajarajeshwarinagar Sub-Division.

According to the complaint, the property owner, N.S. Balachandra Dutta, had obtained building permission for a basement, ground floor and two upper floors. However, the owner allegedly proceeded to construct two additional floors in violation of the sanctioned plan and building bye-laws.

Despite the issuance of notices under Sections 248(1), 248(2) and 248(3) of the BBMP Act, 2020, followed by a confirmation order under Section 356(1) on September 3, 2024, the unauthorised construction was allegedly not removed.

The authority noted that no effective steps had been taken to execute the confirmation order. Despite repeated directions, reminders, and a show-cause notice, the Executive Engineer concerned also failed to submit an action-taken report.

Executive Engineer S.L. Papireddy, who appeared before the authority on Monday (November 16) in response to a summons, stated that the order issued under Section 356(1) had not been communicated to him.

Taking serious note of the continued inaction, the Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner to examine the matter, identify the officials responsible for the lapses, fix accountability and initiate appropriate action against the erring officials.
The Commissioner has been directed to appear in person before the authority on December 7 and submit a detailed report.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 17 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 2 Min Read

📰 Karnataka Lokayukta directs Bengaluru West City Corporation Commissioner to fix accountability for inaction on illegal construction

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The Karnataka Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner of the Bengaluru West City Corporation to identify officials responsible for failing to act against an unauthorised construction in Rajarajeshwari Nagar and initiate appropriate action against those found responsible.

The direction follows a complaint filed by K. Manjunath of Ramachandrapura, alleging that officials of the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), now part of the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s Bengaluru West City Corporation, failed to take action against illegal construction at Site No. 67 in Ward No. 160 of the Rajarajeshwarinagar Sub-Division.

According to the complaint, the property owner, N.S. Balachandra Dutta, had obtained building permission for a basement, ground floor and two upper floors. However, the owner allegedly proceeded to construct two additional floors in violation of the sanctioned plan and building bye-laws.

Despite the issuance of notices under Sections 248(1), 248(2) and 248(3) of the BBMP Act, 2020, followed by a confirmation order under Section 356(1) on September 3, 2024, the unauthorised construction was allegedly not removed.

The authority noted that no effective steps had been taken to execute the confirmation order. Despite repeated directions, reminders, and a show-cause notice, the Executive Engineer concerned also failed to submit an action-taken report.

Executive Engineer S.L. Papireddy, who appeared before the authority on Monday (November 16) in response to a summons, stated that the order issued under Section 356(1) had not been communicated to him.

Taking serious note of the continued inaction, the Lokayukta has directed the Commissioner to examine the matter, identify the officials responsible for the lapses, fix accountability and initiate appropriate action against the erring officials.

The Commissioner has been directed to appear in person before the authority on December 7 and submit a detailed report.

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.
Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.
India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.

Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.

Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.

Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.

India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.

On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

articles.title: Fresh unrest in Bangladesh as garment workers protest, block highways for higher wages
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways

Authorities in Bangladesh on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) deployed more than 1,000 paramilitary personnel as garment workers staged demonstrations and clashed with police in the industrial belt around Dhaka, demanding higher wages and blocking three major highways.

Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, disrupting traffic and causing long tailbacks.
The demonstrations are part of weeks of intermittent protests that began in late October across Bangladesh's major garment-producing areas.
The workers have been demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from the existing Tk 12,500 ($100) to Tk 30,000 ($240), citing rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare.

Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for more than 80% of the country's export earnings, with prolonged disruption threatening production schedules, international buyers' confidence and global apparel supply chains.
In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said it had deployed 42 platoons of personnel in the industrial hubs of Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj. Officials said the personnel were also using drones to maintain surveillance over readymade garment factory workers.

Police said two of the three highways had been cleared, but intermittent blockades continued to cause heavy traffic congestion on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway. "We are working to clear the highways and disperse the protesters," a police spokesperson said.

The industrial unrest also affected factory operations. Police said at least 37 garment factories across the industrial belt were declared closed on Tuesday, while dozens more temporarily suspended production after workers left their workplaces to join demonstrations.

In Dhaka, garment workers gathered in the Darus Salam and Shah Ali police station areas of Mirpur on Tuesday morning and attempted to move towards the Mirpur-10 roundabout, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.

articles.title: Burnham delays tabling of options for U.K.-EU ties
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has delayed unveiling options for long-term ties between the U.K.- and EU The Prime Minister had said in September that he would set out options — including the option of a complete return to the EU — around the U.K.-EU Summit, which is scheduled for Friday.

“This will take time and we will present those options and our assessment of them to inform decisions in the next Parliament,” Mr. Burnham said on Monday at the annual City Hall banquet in the capital’s financial hub.
“At every stage, the British people will be the boss,” he added.

At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer. Mr. Burnham suggested this deal could increase the U.K.’s GDP by 0.4%.

Legislation for the deal will be presented to the U.K. Parliament next week, the Prime Minister said, as he ruled out crossing red lines, i.e., ruling out joining the EU, allowing the “free movement” of EU citizens across the border or taking the U.K. into the EU Customs Union and Single Market during this Parliament (which ends in 2029).

EU Affairs Minister Hamish Falconer said that a U.K.-EU agreement would involve an “exit clause” in case a future U.K. government run by the Conservatives or Reform U.K. undid the deal, the BBC reported. These two opposition parties have said they would undo any agreement reached by Labour. The exit clause it is likely to involve payments to Brussels to set up border infrastructure.
During his speech Mr. Burnham also spoke of reviving the Commonwealth (of which India is also a part) group of nations.
“It is a unique geopolitical forum, not including either the US or China, and yet we have failed to invest energy in modernising the Commonwealth,” he said.
The Prime Minister said Britain would offer countries a structured dialogue in 2027 on its historical role in slavery but would not make financial reparations for it.

“It is basic good manners, if a friend wants to talk about something that is unjust and unresolved, to listen and engage,” he said. Longstanding calls from Caribbean nations for reparations and apologies grew louder in recent weeks, around a visit of King Charles III to the region.

articles.title: Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, eight people arrested
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from

Eight people were detained in central Assam’s Hojai district after they clashed with Forest Department personnel on Monday night (November 16, 2026) during an operation to guide a female elephant back to the jungle it came from.

The Forest officials fired “sera bullets” (pellets) from a pump-action gun to divert the elephant away from a human settlement. Five people were injured in the firing, triggering the mob violence and leaving two personnel injured.
Forest officials claimed three people sustained pellet injuries. The injured, including one of the two personnel, were admitted to a local hospital for treatment.

Divisional Forest Officer Nayan Jyoti Rajbongshi said a herd of elephants from the hills of Karbi Anglong entered the Hawaipur Reserve Forest in Hojai on Monday morning. Barring the female elephant, estimated to be 40 years old, the herd returned to Karbi Anglong a few hours later.
“We received information about the movement of the female elephant, possibly separated from the herd, along a road in a revenue area. We managed to push it into the Hawaipur Reserve Forest,” he said.
However, the elephant emerged from the forest around dusk and headed toward a village. The Forest personnel fired the pellets to drive it away, but some villagers were injured in the process.
“The police brought the situation under control and picked up eight people who clashed with our personnel. The police recorded the statement of our personnel,” Mr. Rajbongshi said.
Wildlife officials said people often obstruct rescue operations by gathering around a wild animal that strays out of a forest.
According to Assam government data tabled in the 126-member Assembly in July, as many as 1,147 people and 246 elephants were killed in human-elephant conflicts in the State since 2016.

In a post in Hindi on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said, “Abki baar, AQI 400-paar. The ‘pravachanmantri’s’ (preaching minister) slogan is coming true when it comes to AQI!”

Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Mr. Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult. Children and the elderly were bearing the brunt of the pollution, while the number of patients in hospitals was rising, he said.
“Slogans were tossed into the air; now the air itself has turned to poison,” he said.
Mr. Modi had used the “Abki baar, 400-paar” slogan during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, seeking a mandate of more than 400 seats for the National Democratic Alliance.

Several air quality monitoring stations in Delhi have recorded AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category (400-500) over the past few days. The city’s average AQI had also crossed the 400-mark on Friday (November 13, 2026).

articles.title: Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space companies to develop High-Resolution Indian Human Settlement Layers (IHSL) across Indian cities.

The three companies, SpacePixxel Technologies Pvt. Ltd. , KaleidEO Space Systems Pvt. Ltd. and Azista Industries Pvt. Ltd. have been selected under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme for Use Case Demonstration by Non-Government Entities (NGEi) to develop IHSL across Indian cities.

These companies will collectively receive seed funding of ₹1.46 crore to develop and demonstrate an indigenous satellite-based system for 3D reconstruction of India’s built environment using monocular imageries.

IN-SPACe said that the initiative, undertaken under the Announcement of Opportunity (AO) for the development of high-resolution IHSL, aims to address the NITI Aayog’s requirement of having an accurate and detailed geospatial data on human settlement which can be used for urban planning, infrastructure development and disaster risk assessment in addition to population assessment.

The selected companies will develop models using Earth Observation data to generate three integrated outputs covering built-up surface and building type, building height, and built-up volume. The deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.
The techniques will be developed at a high spatial resolution using Indian satellite data.

The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, representing distinct urban contexts of a large metropolitan region and a hill city. The pilot project will derive settlement patterns across two time periods, enabling comparisons of urban growth and changes in built-up density over time.

“India’s cities are expanding rapidly, both horizontally and vertically. Effective urban planning requires an accurate understanding of the built environment, but critical data gaps often limit this. This initiative addresses that gap by bringing together Indian satellite data, indigenous technology and clearly defined requirements from government departments. It gives Indian companies an opportunity to develop solutions for real-world urban challenges. More importantly, successful pilots can lay the foundation for scalable, homegrown capabilities that can be deployed across Indian cities,” Dr. Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe, said.

“Starting with Bengaluru and Shimla, this IN-SPACe supported project will provide pathways to build indigenous satellite data on human settlements, allowing recognition of urbanisation as it happens.” said Shamika Ravi, Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)
Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received.

articles.title: Nvidia to reveal first earnings since spy scandal
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis
AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit and the United States to tighten export curbs on chips.
Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

Mr. Huang, perhaps the tech industry's most recognised booster of AI, stepped down on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The scandal has battered shares of Nvidia -- until recently the world's most valuable publicly traded company -- which is at the centre of an AI buildout that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe.

Washington announced new restrictions on Monday (November 16) on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing just before the high-profile APEC summit where U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are set for talks.
Beijing's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests".

The new U.S. export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi's talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, which starts Wednesday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington's new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a U.S. license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under U.S. arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil -- countries the U.S. commerce department says present a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on U.S. hardware not available for export to China.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.summary: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina
articles.keyPoints:
• India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina
• Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.
• The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: CIAL sets up facilitation centre for Sabarimala pilgrims
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to inaugurate the facility on November 17

Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL) has set up a dedicated pilgrim facilitation centre at the airport for Sabarimala pilgrims. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the centre on November 17.

Spread across 5,000 sq. ft., the centre is located near the police aid post, adjacent to the domestic arrival terminal and will remain open round the clock. KSRTC bus services are available to and from the airport from here, with a booking counter set up at the centre. Pilgrims can also book chartered bus services on demand. A dedicated counter for helicopter service bookings has also been arranged.

The other facilities at the centre include a Devaswom help desk, prasadam coupon counter, prepaid taxi booking facility, vegetarian food outlet, and a rest area. A flight information display system has also been installed to provide real-time flight updates. Its proximity to the domestic terminal makes the centre easily accessible to pilgrims, says an official release.
Around 11,000 pilgrims made use of the facilitation centre last year, including those from Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Malaysia, and Singapore, it says.

articles.title: Boy electrocuted by snapped stay wire in Malappuram; Minister orders probe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 13-year-old boy died of electrocution after coming into contact with a snapped stay wire attached to an electric pole in a paddy field in Malappuram on Sunday (November 15).
The deceased, identified as Junaid, son of Shihabudheen of Cherumukku in Tirurangadi, had gone to the field with friends to watch a tractor plough the land, the police said.

Residents said Junaid’s friends tried to rescue him, but the tractor driver stopped them from approaching the wire, saving them from a similar fate. They alleged that officials of the Keralam State Electricity Board (KSEB) took time to disconnect the power supply despite repeated calls for help.
The incident triggered protests by residents who accused KSEB officials of serious negligence.
Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph ordered an immediate inquiry into the incident and directed officials to ensure compensation for the bereaved family.

In a statement, Mr. Joseph said that he had directed the Deputy Chief Engineer of KSEB, Tirurangadi, to submit a factual report immediately. “Strict disciplinary action will be taken against those found responsible for any lapse,” he added.
The Minister said safety inspections would be intensified across the State to prevent the recurrence of such incidents.
Meanwhile, the KSEB, in a statement, apologised for the incident and said that an impartial and detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the accident would be conducted.
The KSEB urged consumers to report electricity-related safety hazards by sending photographs and details through WhatsApp to 94960-10101.

A 13-year-old boy died of electrocution after coming into contact with a snapped stay wire attached to an electric pole in a paddy field in Malappuram on Sunday (November 15).

The deceased, identified as Junaid, son of Shihabudheen of Cherumukku in Tirurangadi, had gone to the field with friends to watch a tractor plough the land, the police said.

Residents said Junaid’s friends tried to rescue him, but the tractor driver stopped them from approaching the wire, saving them from a similar fate. They alleged that officials of the Keralam State Electricity Board (KSEB) took time to disconnect the power supply despite repeated calls for help.

The incident triggered protests by residents who accused KSEB officials of serious negligence.

Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph ordered an immediate inquiry into the incident and directed officials to ensure compensation for the bereaved family.

In a statement, Mr. Joseph said that he had directed the Deputy Chief Engineer of KSEB, Tirurangadi, to submit a factual report immediately. “Strict disciplinary action will be taken against those found responsible for any lapse,” he added.

The Minister said safety inspections would be intensified across the State to prevent the recurrence of such incidents.

Meanwhile, the KSEB, in a statement, apologised for the incident and said that an impartial and detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the accident would be conducted.

The KSEB urged consumers to report electricity-related safety hazards by sending photographs and details through WhatsApp to 94960-10101.

articles.title: My entire life has been a struggle, says Bilkis Bano at GIO conference in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage.

“My entire life has been a struggle,” Bilkis Bano, the Gujarat riots survivor who has emerged as an icon of resilience with her prolonged legal battle for justice, said in Kochi on Sunday (November 15).
Ms. Bano made the compelling remark as she inaugurated the International Conference on Women organised by the State committee of the Girls Islamic Organisation (GIO) in the city.

“Everyone knows my life story, don’t they? There is no need to say anything more about it,” she said in a brief address. Ms. Bano was gang-raped and lost seven members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, in the 2002 riots.
Thanking those who invited her, she said, “May we continue to live with such love and peace every day, staying together all our lives.”

Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage. “The family had to relocate several times, and her rights were denied. They had to repeatedly bring instances of injustice to the attention of those in positions of power. What happened to Bilkis is now known to the entire world. May her struggle inspire every woman to find the strength to raise her voice for her rights,” he said.
The conference was presided over by GIO State president K. Shifana. Jamia Millia Islamia student leader Nousheen Farooq was the chief guest.

Saria Cheruvallil, Professor at Coventry University, UK; Dalia Saleh, researcher at the University of Cambridge; Reem Mahmoud Al Haddad, Palestinian writer and journalist; Jamaat-e-Islami national secretary A. Rahmathunnisa; and Jamaat-e-Islami Keralam ameer P. Mujeeb Rahman were among those who spoke at various sessions.

articles.title: Prince William, Princess Kate to meet Modi in New Delhi this week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The couple will arrive in Mumbai today for the annual Earthshot Prize; the visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry

The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Katherine (Kate), are due to arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening (November 17) at a ceremony in the city. The couple will stay in Mumbai for the duration of their visit, which ends on Wednesday night (November 18, 2026).

The visit will involve events focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly,​ Brian Lara and England captain ​Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by Prince William in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crores) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.
India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody ), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s (November 17, 2026) event .
When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest of 15,000 schools across 24 States.

This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India and Princess Kate’s first major overseas trip since she was treated for cancer in 2024 and had to step back from official duties.

articles.title: M.P. CM announces crop loss survey, financial aid for farmers in rain deficit Alirajpur district
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday announced a crop loss survey in Alirajpur to provide financial assistance to the farmers in the State’s worst rain-deficit district.

Addressing a Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme, marking the birth anniversary of tribal icon Birsa Munda, in Jhobat, the CM announced he was issuing instructions to the District Collector to begin the survey and provide aid to farmers affected by rain deficiency.
“I am issuing directions to the Collector to conduct a survey and help them as per the Revenue Book Circular (RBC) 6-4. You will get money in your accounts from the government,” he said.

At least 11 districts of Madhya Pradesh have experienced severe rainfall deficit, with those in the Nimar and Malwa regions being the worst hit. It severely impacted kharif crops like soybean. Alirajpur, that falls under the Nimar region, recorded nearly 52% lower rainfall than normal. The government, though, has not announced such surveys in other affected districts, even as officials claim that discussions on relief measures are going on.

Earlier in the day, Chief Minister and Governor Mangubhai Patel inaugurated ₹1,353.18 crore Dahi Micro Lift Irrigation Project in Dhar’s Dahi, which aims to provide irrigation through Narmada water to 47,000 hectares of agricultural land across 84 villages in Dhar and and 42 in Alirajpur districts. According to government officials, about a lakh farmers are likely to benefit directly from the project’s permanent irrigation facility.
Last month, Mr. Yadav had launched another micro-lift irrigation project worth around ₹2,400-crore in Dhar’s Sardarpur.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices
India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 16 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 2 Min Read

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance

The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices

India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.

While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.

India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.

The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”

Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”

The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.

Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.

articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The RBI has reportedly proposed a ₹50 lakh sub-limit within the $250,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap to curb dollar outflows and protect the rupee

The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A six-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted by an eight-year-old classmate in a classroom in Panchkula, with CCTV footage capturing the attack. The incident raises concerns about school safety, supervision, and the influence of violent video games on children

The school’s auto-rickshaw arrived at its usual time around noon on October 28. Homemaker Aarti (name changed to protect privacy) took a quick, reassuring look at her six-year-old daughter’s uniform and schoolbag before waving her off with a smile. However, at 3:30 p.m., when the auto-rickshaw driver went to pick her up from her school in Haryana ’s Panchkula district, the girl was nowhere to be found. Her bag was kept at the school’s reception area.

The driver informed her family, who live just five minutes away from the school, and her father came rushing. As he called out her name, his voice grew louder with every frantic step towards the school building. He asked the teachers about his daughter’s whereabouts, and they joined him in his search. Soon, a boy approached him, asked his daughter’s name and confirmed whether he was looking for her. When the father nodded, the boy led him to a classroom on the first floor, telling him that someone had beaten her up.

Political & National Report: Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Prince William, Princess Kate to meet PM Modi in New Delhi this week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The couple will arrive in Mumbai today for the annual Earthshot Prize ceremony; the visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry

The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Catherine (Kate), are due to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday. The couple will arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening at a ceremony in the city.

The couple, who were originally scheduled to spend their entire visit in Mumbai, will now conclude it with a meeting with Mr. Modi. Their schedule was changed on Sunday after Mr. Modi’s travel plans were confirmed, the Sunday Times reported. The Prime Minister is due to return from the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Summit in the Philippines on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly, Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by the Prince in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crore) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.
India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody ), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s event.
When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest among 15,000 schools across 24 States.

“The future of the U.K.-India partnership will not be shaped by our governments alone, it will be shaped by our people and this visit is a wonderful opportunity to celebrate those deep personal connections between our countries,” said Ben Mellor, Acting British High Commissioner to India, according to PTI.

The couple will arrive in Mumbai today for the annual Earthshot Prize ceremony; the visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry

The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Catherine (Kate), are due to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday. The couple will arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening at a ceremony in the city.

The couple, who were originally scheduled to spend their entire visit in Mumbai, will now conclude it with a meeting with Mr. Modi. Their schedule was changed on Sunday after Mr. Modi’s travel plans were confirmed, the Sunday Times reported. The Prime Minister is due to return from the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Summit in the Philippines on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly, Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by the Prince in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crore) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.

India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody ), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s event.

When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest among 15,000 schools across 24 States.

“The future of the U.K.-India partnership will not be shaped by our governments alone, it will be shaped by our people and this visit is a wonderful opportunity to celebrate those deep personal connections between our countries,” said Ben Mellor, Acting British High Commissioner to India, according to PTI.

This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India and the Princess’s first major overseas trip since she was treated for cancer in 2024 and had to step back from official duties.

articles.title: West Bengal BJP president alleges conversions at missionary schools; draws flak
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the first time a senior State BJP leader has made remarks about the community, even as Christian groups have protested against attacks on churches

West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) chief Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 15, 2026) warned Christian missionary schools in the State over alleged religious conversions taking place at these institutions.

“If in Christian missionary schools there are anti-India activities on the grounds of religion and colour, we will not allow such schools to continue. In one school, an authority has kept the flag of Pakistan on the table... Another reputed school has asked one of its teachers not to attend the school wearing saffron saris,” Mr. Bhattacharya claimed at an event.

This is the first time a senior State BJP leader has made remarks about the community, even as Christian groups have protested against attacks on churches. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP), an umbrella forum of Christian organisations, urged Mr. Bhattacharya to publicly name the schools.

“If anyone has indeed engaged in such conduct, it is highly condemnable. However, making sweeping generalisations about Christian missionary schools in public without naming the institutions involved is irresponsible, condemnable and dangerous,” said BCP founding secretary Herod Mullick.

Earlier in the day, CM Suvendu Adhikari accused the previous Trinamool Congress government of considering only Muslims as a minority community, asserting that Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains also qualify as religious minorities.

articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.
Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.
India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

articles.title: As diabetes spikes in Kashmir, the health lens turns to the fabled wazwan
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living has been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns persist largely unchanged, the doctor-authors of Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir say

The Kashmiri wazwan , an array of dishes adding up to 4,500-5,500 calories partaken during festivals and weddings, is one of the key cultural factors contributing to a spike in cases of diabetes in Kashmir, experts said.

Kashmir’s social life is organised around large, meat-centred feasts, most visibly the wazwan served at weddings or on Eid. Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir , a book released on World Diabetes Day (November 14), said the multi-course meal can run to over 30 mutton and chicken preparations, with the calorie intake “several times the average daily requirement”.

“Such exposure accumulates rather than occurs in isolation, and repeated post-prandial glucose and lipid excursions of this magnitude plausibly contribute to the region’s rising dysglycaemia burden,” the book, co-authored by endocrinologists Mohammad Hayat Bhat and Shahnawaz Mir, and cardiologist Nasir Shams, stated.
Degchis (traditional heavy-bottomed cooking pots) filled with wazwan dishes at a wedding feast in Srinagar. | Photo Credit: Reuters

J&K has witnessed a spike in the incidence of diabetes in the past three years. The Union Territory screened more than 2.15 million people for diabetes; 48,623 individuals have been diagnosed to have diabetes, according to data from the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. In 2025-2026, 2.84 million people were screened and 85,948 were found to have diabetes. “In the past three years, J&K added 2.18 lakh new patients to its diabetes burden,” the Ministry’s data suggested.
Apart from more universally seen factors, including poor physical activity and consumption of tobacco, the book identifies Kashmir’s unique lifestyle among the contributing factors.

“Kashmir’s daily plate remains rice-centric with rice typically supplying the bulk of meal volume and carbohydrate load. Large portions of rice translate directly into high postprandial glycaemic load,” it said.

“Type 2 diabetes prevalence in Kashmir has risen sharply within a single generation. A survey in 1999 found known diabetes in just 1.89% of adults, with 4.25% undiagnosed. Recent Indian Council of Medical Research-INDIA data show 7.8% prevalence,” the authors said, attributing the rising incidence of Type 2 diabetes to lifestyle in Kashmir.

The book noted that such a rapid shift cannot reflect genetic change. “It points instead to a compressed nutrition and lifestyle transition, as subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living have been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns — rice-centric meals, salt tea, preserved winter foods, and elaborate festive feasting — persist largely unchanged,” the experts said.

They also attributed the rise in cases of diabetes to Kashmir’s winters. “The glycaemic and fat load of the traditional meat and generous portion sizes do not act in isolation. Their convergence with a pronounced winter sedentary period appears to produce a compounding rather than merely additive metabolic burden across the Kashmiri annual cycle, in which periods of highest intake coincide with the lowest levels of expenditure,” they added.

A man accused of opening fire at a police constable at Santiniketan in West Bengal 's Birbhum district on Friday (November 13, 2026) was killed in a gunfight with the law enforcers on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a senior officer said.
Ratan Sheikh was killed after he opened fire at a police team while trying to evade arrest at a brick kiln in Nanoor in the same district.
