articles.title: Funds sought to clear traffic gridlocks on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Motorists, residents’ and merchants’ bodies have been demanding steps to clear traffic bottlenecks on the stretch that runs parallel to the Palarivattom-Kundannur NH bypass, considering the immense potential the road holds to decongest the bypass. On widening Vennala Junction, Uma Thomas, MLA, says apart from widening the junction’s bell mouth, land might have to be acquired at approximately one metre width from either side of the junction to ensure smooth flow of traffic

With plans afoot to widen the severely bottlenecked Vennala Junction under a ₹1 crore project, demand is rife to widen the two narrow and similarly choked trijunctions on either side of the junction and also Alinchuvadu Junction where traffic snarls are the norm.
Vehicles jostling for space at the congested Alinchuvadu Junction. | Photo Credit: H. VIBHU

Apart from motorists, residents’ and merchants’ bodies have over the years been demanding that the State government allot funds to clear traffic bottlenecks on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road that runs parallel to the Palarivattom-Kundannur NH bypass stretch, considering the immense potential the road held to decongest the bypass.

Over the past few years, serpentine traffic snarls have been the norm at Vennala Junction and at the three other junctions on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road that is increasingly being used by IT professionals and others who travel from the NH bypass towards Infopark, other places in Kakkanad, and Thripunithura, said Sabu Koroth, councillor representing Vennala (Division 38) in the Kochi Corporation.
The bottlenecked Vennala Junction. Traffic snarls have been the norm at the Junction for years. | Photo Credit: H. VIBHU

“A committee comprising people’s representatives and others was constituted following a stakeholder meeting that was held recently to collate suggestions from members of the public on decongesting Vennala Junction. The suggestions would be submitted to Thrikkakara MLA Uma Thomas and later on to the District Collector, based on which a master plan to decongest the region is set to be readied,” he said.

It is high time adequate funds were allotted to widen the three other extremely narrow junctions (Alinchuvadu, V-Guard Junction, and Sundarimukku) as well to ensure smooth and safe movement of vehicles and pedestrians in the corridor, Mr. Koroth said.

On the proposal to widen Vennala Junction, the MLA said that apart from widening the junction’s bell mouth, land might have to be acquired at approximately one metre width from either side of the junction to ensure smooth flow of traffic.
The bell mouth of the junctions north and south of Vennala too must be widened for commuters to make optimal use of the road corridor, suggested Rajesh Vennala, a social worker from the area.

This is crucial since traffic would increase manifold when MG Road-Pullepady-Thammanam-NH bypass road that is slated to be four-laned, is extended further eastward from Chakkaraparambu on the NH bypass to Seaport-Airport Road through largely puramboke lands, he said.

📰 Funds sought to clear traffic gridlocks on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road in Keralam’s Kochi

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Motorists, residents’ and merchants’ bodies have been demanding steps to clear traffic bottlenecks on the stretch that runs parallel to the Palarivattom-Kundannur NH bypass, considering the immense potential the road holds to decongest the bypass. On widening Vennala Junction, Uma Thomas, MLA, says apart from widening the junction’s bell mouth, land might have to be acquired at approximately one metre width from either side of the junction to ensure smooth flow of traffic

With plans afoot to widen the severely bottlenecked Vennala Junction under a ₹1 crore project, demand is rife to widen the two narrow and similarly choked trijunctions on either side of the junction and also Alinchuvadu Junction where traffic snarls are the norm.

Vehicles jostling for space at the congested Alinchuvadu Junction. | Photo Credit: H. VIBHU

Apart from motorists, residents’ and merchants’ bodies have over the years been demanding that the State government allot funds to clear traffic bottlenecks on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road that runs parallel to the Palarivattom-Kundannur NH bypass stretch, considering the immense potential the road held to decongest the bypass.

Over the past few years, serpentine traffic snarls have been the norm at Vennala Junction and at the three other junctions on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road that is increasingly being used by IT professionals and others who travel from the NH bypass towards Infopark, other places in Kakkanad, and Thripunithura, said Sabu Koroth, councillor representing Vennala (Division 38) in the Kochi Corporation.

The bottlenecked Vennala Junction. Traffic snarls have been the norm at the Junction for years. | Photo Credit: H. VIBHU

“A committee comprising people’s representatives and others was constituted following a stakeholder meeting that was held recently to collate suggestions from members of the public on decongesting Vennala Junction. The suggestions would be submitted to Thrikkakara MLA Uma Thomas and later on to the District Collector, based on which a master plan to decongest the region is set to be readied,” he said.

It is high time adequate funds were allotted to widen the three other extremely narrow junctions (Alinchuvadu, V-Guard Junction, and Sundarimukku) as well to ensure smooth and safe movement of vehicles and pedestrians in the corridor, Mr. Koroth said.

On the proposal to widen Vennala Junction, the MLA said that apart from widening the junction’s bell mouth, land might have to be acquired at approximately one metre width from either side of the junction to ensure smooth flow of traffic.

The bell mouth of the junctions north and south of Vennala too must be widened for commuters to make optimal use of the road corridor, suggested Rajesh Vennala, a social worker from the area.

This is crucial since traffic would increase manifold when MG Road-Pullepady-Thammanam-NH bypass road that is slated to be four-laned, is extended further eastward from Chakkaraparambu on the NH bypass to Seaport-Airport Road through largely puramboke lands, he said.

articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their ​main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.
"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."
There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

articles.title: Six days of restrictions in Kulgam reminiscent of 1990s, people facing collective hardships: PDP's Sartaj Madani
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Parts of south Kashmir’s Kulgam were placed under restrictions following a terrorist attack on a CRPF checkpoint at Akhran

A six-day-long anti-terror operation in villages of south Kashmir’s Kulgam on Monday (November 16, 2026) drew criticism from the Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), which said restrictions on the movement of people, particularly in Akhran and its adjoining areas, “were creating an atmosphere of fear, uncertainty and collective hardship”.
Parts of south Kashmir’s Kulgam were placed under restrictions following a terrorist attack on a CRPF checkpoint at Akhran on November 11.

“The situation is increasingly reminiscent of the difficult days of the 1990s. We cannot allow the people of Kashmir to be pushed back into an era they have suffered immensely to overcome. Let me make it absolutely clear: security must never be compromised, but neither can human rights, dignity and the fundamental freedoms of common citizens be compromised in the name of security,” said PDP leader Sartaj Madani.

Residents of several villages in Kulgam alleged that security forces have set up checkpoints at the exit and entry points of several localities since October 11. Locals alleged they were being “denied free movement”. Besides, searches of houses were also being carried out to trace the attackers, who fled from the spot.

“Security measures must be intelligence-driven, proportionate and sensitive to the hardships faced by the civilian population. The innocent must not be made to pay the price for the actions of perpetrators,” said Mr. Madani.

Hitting out at the ruling National Conference (NC), Mr. Madani said, “Equally disappointing is the deafening silence of the elected government. People voted for a popular government hoping their voices would be heard, their rights protected, and their concerns addressed. Today, when people are facing restrictions and uncertainty, where is that government? Where are its representatives? Not even a meaningful statement of concern has come from those who sought the people’s mandate.”

He said the government cannot claim the people’s mandate in elections and disappear when the people need it most. “Silence in the face of public hardship is not governance; it is an abdication of responsibility. We demand an immediate review of restrictions, relief for affected residents, protection of civilian rights and a clear public response from the government,” said Mr. Madani.

He said the people of Kashmir have endured enough. “They deserve security without fear, governance without silence, and dignity without conditions. A popular mandate is a responsibility to stand with the people, not a licence to remain silent when they suffer,” the PDP leader added.

articles.title: Bat, ball and ‘kulhad’ chai: Prince William and Princess Kate’s regal morning in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Details of the event were so closely guarded that the students taking part did not know who the visiting dignitaries were

Britain’s Prince William and Princess Catherine got a taste of Mumbai street life on Monday (November 16, 2026) as they played ‘gully cricket’ with schoolgirls and cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar on the first day of their three-day India visit.
The event was held on N Morarji Road in Ballard Estate, where old sandstone buildings with small balconies give the area its colonial-era feel.
The royal couple, welcomed with the traditional dhol tasha, also had “cutting chai” (a half-serving of tea) served in earthen ‘kulhads’ at a tea stall under a large banyan tree.

Prince William, Princess Catherine of Wales along with Sachin Tendulkar play Gully cricket with youth at Ballard Estate in Mumbai on Monday, November 16, 2026. The couple arrived in ​Mumbai to attend the annual ‌Earthshot Prize awards, marking the ​Princess of Wales' most high-profile ⁠overseas visit since undergoing treatment for cancer in 2024. Video: @EmmanualYogini
Gully cricket is a form of the game played in narrow lanes because of space constraints.
Details of the event were so closely guarded that the students taking part did not know who the visiting dignitaries were.

Batul Fatima Shaikh and Umme Hani, both Class 8 students of Anjuman Islam’s Begum Sharifa Kalsekar Girls English School in Nagpada, said their teachers had announced an event on November 16 and invited interested students to enrol.
“Since it was Diwali vacation, we enrolled. But we were not sure who was coming here,” Shaikh said.
When told that the visitor was the Prince of Wales, she looked surprised, smiled and said, “Oh! I have read about him.”
This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India, following their visit in April 2016.

Britain’s Prince William and Princess Catherine got a taste of Mumbai street life on Monday (November 16, 2026) as they played ‘gully cricket’ with schoolgirls and cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar on the first day of their three-day India visit.

The event was held on N Morarji Road in Ballard Estate, where old sandstone buildings with small balconies give the area its colonial-era feel.

The royal couple, welcomed with the traditional dhol tasha, also had “cutting chai” (a half-serving of tea) served in earthen ‘kulhads’ at a tea stall under a large banyan tree.

Prince William, Princess Catherine of Wales along with Sachin Tendulkar play Gully cricket with youth at Ballard Estate in Mumbai on Monday, November 16, 2026. Gully cricket is a form of the game played in narrow lanes because of space constraints.

Details of the event were so closely guarded that the students taking part did not know who the visiting dignitaries were.

Batul Fatima Shaikh and Umme Hani, both Class 8 students of Anjuman Islam’s Begum Sharifa Kalsekar Girls English School in Nagpada, said their teachers had announced an event on November 16 and invited interested students to enrol.

“Since it was Diwali vacation, we enrolled. But we were not sure who was coming here,” Shaikh said.

When told that the visitor was the Prince of Wales, she looked surprised, smiled and said, “Oh! I have read about him.”

articles.title: Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize 2026: All you need to know
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The sixth Earthshot Prize, founded by Britain’s Prince William to promote innovative climate change solutions, will be presented in Mumbai on November 17, 2026

Britain’s Prince William and Princess Catherine (Kate) has arrived in Mumbai for a three-day visit to India as part of the sixth edition of The Earthshot Prize. They will join 5,000 guests, including environmental innovators, business leaders, philanthropists and celebrities from across the world in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) to celebrate the prestigious environmental awards.

This marks the royal couples’ first joint overseas engagement since Ms. Kate announced her cancer diagnosis in 2024, also her first Earthshot Prize since 2022, when the ceremony was held in Boston, United States.
The couple’s return to India comes nearly a decade after their previous joint visit to the country in 2016, when they also travelled to Bhutan.
The Earthshot Prize is a prestigious environmental award, a project that was launched by Prince William in 2020, and is supported by a global coalition of philanthropists and organisations.

It aims to encourage innovative solutions to climate change and other major environmental challenges such as air pollution, waste, ocean conservation and the loss of biodiversity. It also aims to recognise 50 winners over a 10-year period.

Every year, five winners are selected from 15 global finalists, with each winner receiving £1 million (approx. ₹12.5 crore) to encourage their work and turn bold environmental ideas into actual impact. In November 2026, the sixth edition of the award arrives in Mumbai, also the first time the ceremony is held in India.

The Earthshot Awards operate on the belief that human ingenuity, innovation and optimism can help repair the planet. Each year, 15 climate solutions are shortlisted across five categories known as Earthshots: Protect and Restore Nature, Clean Our Air, Revive Our Ocean, Build a Waste Free World, and Fix Our Climate.

Under the ‘Protect and Restore Nature’ category, Bhutan’s Princess Chimi Yangzom Wangchuck and Karma Tenzin, senior forestry officer, have been shortlisted for their work in protecting the Himalayan forests which help the water systems that sustain 1.6 billion people downstream across South Asia.

Sam Murray, CEO of ‘The Indigenous Alliance’, has been shortlisted for supporting rangers caring for 270 million hectares of Australian desert. Dr Jodi Hilty, president and chief scientist, and Chief Harlan Schilling of the Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative have been shortlisted for reconnecting 3,400 km of wilderness across Canada and the United States.
Under the ‘Clean Our Air’ category, Suman Mishra, managing director and CEO of Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, has been shortlisted for building affordable electric rickshaws.

articles.title: Four months after launch, Kochi’s third Ro-Ro vessel remains idle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: One of the existing two vessels remains out of service after developing a snag owing to long-overdue maintenance

More than four months after the third Ro-Ro vessel of the Kochi Corporation was launched with much fanfare , it is yet to commence commercial operations, even as one of the existing two vessels remains out of service after developing a snag owing to long-overdue maintenance.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan formally launched the new Ro-Ro vessel, constructed at the Cochin Shipyard Limited, on July 12. It was expected to begin commercial operations shortly thereafter, paving the way for the maintenance of the other two vessels on a rotational basis so that at least two vessels would remain operational at any given point.

Mayor V.K. Minimol attributed the delay to the completion of the process of forming a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for handing over the operation and maintenance of all three Ro-Ro vessels to a new agency, replacing the Kerala Shipping & Inland Navigation Corporation Ltd (KSINC).

“We have now decided to entrust the operation of the new Ro-Ro vessel to KSINC as a stop-gap arrangement and send the vessel already in disrepair for maintenance. Once the SPV is formed, a new agency will be selected through a tendering process to operate all three of the Corporation’s Ro-Ro vessels,” she said.

The Corporation forwarded the draft agreement to KSINC for operating the new vessel last Friday. KSINC is likely to have it vetted by its legal department and send it back to the Corporation, following which it will be formally signed. With only a single vessel now in operation, causing great hardship to commuters on the Vypeen-Fort Kochi route, the launch of the new vessel could not be delayed any further.

“The repair of the vessel that has been taken out of service may take time since it has to be attended to by suppliers of the imported spares. We will send back the draft agreement for the operation of the new vessel after legal vetting within a day or two,” said KSINC sources.

Meanwhile, regular commuters on the stretch insist that even operating three Ro-Ro vessels would not fully address the mobility challenges along the route and have criticised the Corporation for delaying the operation of the third vessel for the sake of forming the SPV. They also fear a situation in which, even after the introduction of the new vessel, operations would effectively be restricted to two vessels, as one may frequently remain out of service for one reason or another.

“What we need is more boat services by the State Water Transport Department. A boat service on a trial basis could be operated from Goshree Junction to Kamalakkadavu, which could then be extended to more points, including Mattancherry and Thoppumpady. Many jetties along the Mattancherry-Thoppumpady stretch remain in a state of neglect and could be renovated and dredged to facilitate these boat services,” said Francis Chammany, president of the Vypeen-Fort Kochi Passengers’ Association.

“We have now decided to entrust the operation of the new Ro-Ro vessel to KSINC as a stop-gap arrangement and send the vessel already in disrepair for maintenance. Once the SPV is formed, a new agency will be selected through a tendering process to operate all three of the Corporation’s Ro-Ro vessels,” she said.

The Corporation forwarded the draft agreement to KSINC for operating the new vessel last Friday. KSINC is likely to have it vetted by its legal department and send it back to the Corporation, following which it will be formally signed. With only a single vessel now in operation, causing great hardship to commuters on the Vypeen-Fort Kochi route, the launch of the new vessel could not be delayed any further.

A boat service on a trial basis could be operated from Goshree Junction to Kamalakkadavu, which could then be extended to more points, including Mattancherry and Thoppumpady. articles.title: Seminar at MCEME-Secunderabad explores indigenous space capabilities for military applications
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Military College of Electronics and Mechanical Engineering (MCEME), Secunderabad, organised a seminar on ‘Space as a Military Domain’ on Saturday, bringing together senior military officers, academicians and representatives of the private sector to deliberate on the growing importance of space in modern warfare and the need to strengthen India’s indigenous military space capabilities.

Lt. Gen. I.S. Rathore, MCEME Commandant, stressed the need to develop resilient space capabilities and achieve technological self-reliance through greater collaboration among the Armed Forces, scientific institutions and industry. He said the seminar provided an important platform for exchanging ideas and building partnerships to advance indigenous military space capabilities, in line with the Indian Army’s Decade of Transformation and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

The first session, on ‘Space as a Warfighting Domain’, was moderated by Lt. Gen. K. Surendra Nath (retired) and examined geopolitical competition, deterrence, military power, space situational awareness and emerging threats.

The second session focused on ‘ Indigenous Military Space Capabilities in India ’ and featured a fireside discussion involving representatives of the Telangana government, space-sector companies Skyroot and Sanyark, and start-ups GalaxEye and VyomIC. The third session, ‘Emerging Space Technologies for Military Operations’, explored the use of quantum technology to secure space communications, satellite-based imagery for surveillance, and the development of indigenous satellites and their military applications.

articles.title: European Union nations to unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a so-called "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the EU cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules

articles.title: In reversal, U.S. to fund UN military support in Somalia for another year
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The United States will renew support to international military operations in Somalia, the State Department told AFP on Sunday (November 15, 2026), reversing cuts that had threatened the survival of a coalition fighting Islamist insurgents in the country.

Washington had stopped funding the United Nations Support Office for Somalia (UNSOS) — which provides crucial logistics to African Union military operations — and had given it until the end of 2027 to shut down entirely.

The Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab has been fighting the Somali government for two decades and continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite the African Union military campaign, which was unlikely to be able to continue without UNSOS support.
Washington had expressed frustration with the Somali government's lack of progress against Al-Shabaab and the persistent political chaos in the country as reasons for cutting the funding.

But on Sunday (November 15, 2026), the U.S. State Department said that after consideration, the United States has decided to "support a one-year renewal of the mandates" for both UNSOS and the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM).
A foreign diplomatic source working on Somalia told AFP the return of US support was welcome but that the sudden swings in policy were "madness".

The source, who requested anonymity as they were not authorised to speak publicly on the matter, expressed shock that Washington did not use the promise of renewed funding to put pressure on the Somali government, which has lately descended into fresh in-fighting and political chaos that are undermining the campaign against the insurgents.

Last week, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud fired the chief justice of the Supreme Court as it was about to rule against the extension of his term in office, which it said was illegal, and which has triggered violent clashes with Opposition parties and regional leaders.
Mohamud has tried to move Somalia towards fully democratic elections, but sparked uproar when he pushed through constitutional changes in March that gave him an extra year in office.

The group claimed last month it had killed hundreds of elite Somali soldiers in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region -- potentially one of its deadliest attacks in years, although the government has not released a death toll.

articles.title: India, Egypt discuss steps to boost trade, address non-tariff barriers
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two countries have decided to set up a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a PTA or FTA to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries

India and Egypt have discussed ways to reduce non-tariff barriers, facilitate customs processes, strengthen standards and improve market access with an aim to nearly double bilateral trade to $12 billion, an official statement said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

The two countries have decided to set up a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) or Free Trade Agreement (FTA) to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries.
Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics
India, U.S. agreed on preferential market access for Indian goods in America: Goyal
Besides, the two countries deliberated on resolving issues affecting business operations, including product registrations and trade-related regulatory procedures.

These issues figured during the India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meet, which was co-chaired by Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal and Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, in Cairo on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The committee provided an opportunity to review existing trade ties, assess challenges faced by businesses and identify new areas for closer collaboration.

"Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of $12 billion. They emphasised the need to diversify trade, promote value-added exports and address trade-related challenges," the Commerce Ministry said.
Currently, the bilateral trade is at $6.5 billion and both sides are targeting to double it in the coming years.
The discussions also focused on strengthening business exchanges and encouraging joint manufacturing and investment, it said.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo six months into response
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016
Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, the disease remains out of control and efforts to contain it are faltering.

More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to Government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year.

By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. It has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces, moving at a pace aid groups have likened to wildfire.
New hotspots continue to emerge, stretching an already strained health care system.

Community transmission remains high. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, 80% of new cases are being detected outside health surveillance, meaning most infections have not been tracked by authorities.
Experts warn of wider spread as Ebola outbreak reaches plateau
DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
One-third of deaths occur at home or elsewhere in the community, where burials and other procedures are often conducted without specialist supervision, increasing the risk of transmission.

articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

​The World Health Organisation warned on Friday (November 13, 2026) of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza, with worse expected after ‌heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

“The numbers ​already show the pressure. Acute respiratory infections are 33,000 cases higher than at ⁠the same time last year,” Dr. Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told reporters in Geneva from Jerusalem.

Poor living conditions and severe overcrowding are driving up infections as Gaza’s population ‌is squeezed into an ever-smaller area, WHO said. The crunch has worsened as the Israeli military expands its control by advancing the “Yellow Line” — a demarcation established under ‌October’s U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
“That means people are living in more crowded conditions, where of course ‌the ⁠spread between humans of a virus is much more prone to spread,” Ms. Van ⁠De Weerdt explained.

The Israeli military told Reuters the Yellow Line aims to protect Israeli civilians and army troops from threats and that adjustments to its location follow the ceasefire agreement and international law, and are not intended ​to harm the civilian population.
“The IDF categorically ‌rejects the claim that it operates to deliberately reduce the area available to the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.”

COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, said that more than 93,000 tents and over 8,600 trucks carrying tarpaulin sheets, blankets and winter clothing ‌have entered Gaza since the Board of Peace, UN agencies and NGOs launched ​the winterisation plan. Equipment intended for the reconstruction of Gaza will be permitted to enter only after Hamas has been fully disarmed, it added.
Last week ⁠COGAT said that it had stepped up efforts to improve sanitary conditions before the heavy rain, in coordination with international organisations.
Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher.
“It is shocking that just a few days of rain really showed us what the coming months will bring. And winter has not even fully set in. The worst really is yet to come,” Ms. Van De Weerdt said.

“The numbers ​already show the pressure. Acute respiratory infections are 33,000 cases higher than at ⁠the same time last year,” Dr. Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told reporters in Geneva from Jerusalem.

“That means people are living in more crowded conditions, where of course ‌the ⁠spread between humans of a virus is much more prone to spread,” Ms. Van ⁠De Weerdt explained.

“The IDF categorically ‌rejects the claim that it operates to deliberately reduce the area available to the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.”

Equipment intended for the reconstruction of Gaza will be permitted to enter only after Hamas has been fully disarmed, it added.

Last week ⁠COGAT said that it had stepped up efforts to improve sanitary conditions before the heavy rain, in coordination with international organisations.

articles.title: Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Two celestial bodies—Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua—are a close pair of ancient quasars challenging ideas about early black hole growth

In the Hawaiian language, Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua means “two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe”. It is a nickname astronomers have given to a strange new discovery: an unusual pair of quasars that are also closer to each other than thought possible.

A quasar is the extremely bright centre of a galaxy, where a black hole is drawing in and heating up gases, causing them to emit radiation. The pair is unusual because it existed when the universe was only 900 million years old.

The official designation of Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is J1602+4228AB. Astronomers first spotted the brighter of the pair in 2004, and later the James Webb Space Telescope discovered the second one nearby. Finally, scientists used the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii to study both quasars together.
The quasars are separated by only 18,100 light-years, which is extremely tight for powerful objects of this nature.

Today, astronomers around the world are struggling to explain how black holes could have grown so large within the first billion years of the universe. The black hole in one of the quasars weighs a whopping 1.5 billion solar masses. One hypothesis is that young galaxies merged and funnelled copious amounts of gases towards their central black holes, feeding their growth.

Another is that the gravity of a galaxy lying between the earth and a quasar could bend the quasar’s light, making one object appear as two. This possibility remains to be eliminated — or confirmed — as astronomers continue studying Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.

articles.title: Keralam’s orchids endure from highway trees to salt-sprayed shores
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A rescue-and-relocation project has saved over 27,000 native orchids from roadside trees felled in Keralam, and more than 71% were still alive, ​5,224 had flowered, and 1,934 had produced capsules after one to two years, offering a low-cost model for conservation
With their dazzling colours and ambrosial aromas, orchids are one of earth’s most distinctive flowering plant families.
They are found on every continent except Antarctica and count over 29,500 native species worldwide.
According to Orchids of India: A Pictorial Guide (2019), published by the Botanical Survey of India, Keralam accounts for more than a third of the 307 endemic orchids reported from India.
The State’s native orchid density is comparable to South American countries like Costa Rica, Viswambharan Sarasan, a research leader at the Royal Botanic Gardens in the U.K., said.
But habitat loss and fragmentation are increasingly threatening the State’s orchid diversity.
“As a child, I saw these orchids on coconut palms in our backyard [in Keralam],” he said. “But now they are disappearing from everywhere.”
However, according to Dr. Sarasan, relocating orchids from development sites or disturbed areas can reduce these losses.

Over the last three years, under Dr. Sarasan’s leadership, a research team at the KSCSTE-Malabar Botanical Garden and Institute for Plant Sciences in Calicut has rescued more than 27,000 native orchids growing on trees from being destroyed in road-widening activities in the State.

“I went to Kerala six, seven years ago, pitching this idea of growing orchids in large hubs where people congregate, such as the Napier Museum or the Kanakakunnu Palace in Thiruvananthapuram,” Dr. Sarasan, who hails from the capital city of Keralam, said.

With funding from the Royal Society International Exchanges programme, the project aimed to collect orchids from Keralam’s forests and rural areas. “However, we quickly realised there isn’t much diversity in the south,” he said.

articles.title: Bilkis Bano case: Supreme Court suspends sentence, grants bail to two convicts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: "Having heard the parties, it suffices to state that the appellants have been incarcerated for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law," says Supreme Court

The Supreme Court has suspended the life sentences of two convicts in the case of the gangrape of Bilkis Bano and the murder of seven of her family members during the 2002 riots in Gujarat and granted them bail.
A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and P.B. Varale noted that Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya had been incarcerated for more than 17 years.

"Having heard the parties, it suffices to state that the appellants have been incarcerated for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law," the apex court said in its October 28 order, which has now been uploaded.

"In view of the above and considering the issues involved in this appeal, we suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellants on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court," the bench added.

Arguing that the two men have been incarcerated for more than 17 years, senior advocate Siddharth Luthra submitted that one of the convicts had not been named in the FIR and was implicated after nearly three years following the 2002 riots.

Additional Solicitor General Raja Thakre vehemently opposed the plea and said the High Court and the trial court have taken into consideration the relevant material brought on record, especially as the offence committed is so serious.

Bilkis Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while trying to escape the horror of the communal riots that broke out after the Godhra train burning incident in February 2002. Her three-year-old daughter was among the seven family members killed.
The two convicts, Mordhiya and Joshi, are among the 11 whose remission was quashed by the Supreme Court in 2024.
The other convicts in the case are Govind Nai, Ramesh Chandana, Mitesh Bhatt, Bakabhai Vohania, Kesarbhai Vohania, Jaswant Nai, Radheshyam Shah, Rajubhai Soni and Shailesh Bhatt.

Joshi and Mordhiya were convicted by the trial court under Sections 143 (unlawful assembly), 147 (rioting), 302 (murder) read with Sections 376 (rape) of the Indian Penal Code and were sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life with fine.

articles.title: PM Modi arrives in Philippines to attend two key regional summits
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Manila on November 16-17 to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 16, 2026) arrived in the Philippines to attend two key summits, aiming to strengthen ties with Southeast Asian and East Asian nations and to discuss regional and global challenges.
Mr. Modi will participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on Tuesday (November 15). He is there at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

“At the ASEAN-India Summit, I look forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and give further momentum to our shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity,” he added.
Talking about The East Asia Summit, Mr. Modi said that it ‘provides an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges’.
“I look forward to exchanging views with participating leaders on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific,” the Prime Minister said.
Mr. Modi also said he looks forward to interacting with the vibrant Indian community in the Philippines ‘whose contributions strengthen the bonds of friendship between our two countries’.
“I am confident that the visit will impart new energy to India’s partnership with ASEAN and reinforce our collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific,” he added.
A meeting of the leaders of the Quad group — comprising the U.S., India, Australia and Japan — is scheduled to be held in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit, a senior U.S. official said.

The meeting of the Quad leaders, the first in two years, will bring together Prime Minister Narendra Modi, U.S. President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
The last meeting of Quad leaders was chaired by then U.S. President Joe Biden in Delaware on September 21, 2024.

articles.title: Noted agricultural scientist K. Prabhakaran Nair dies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He made immense contributions to sustainable agriculture, soil science and agronomy, having spent decades conducting research in the field
K. Prabhakaran Nair, agricultural scientist, passed away at his residence in Kozhikode, Keralam, on Monday (November 16, 2026). He was 88.

Mr. Nair began his international research career with a post-doctoral research fellowship in Belgium. He earned his PhD in agronomy, specialising in soil fertility and plant nutrition, from New Delhi’s Indian Agricultural Research Institute in 1965.

He made immense contributions to sustainable agriculture, soil science and agronomy, having spent decades conducting research in the field. Mr. Nair travelled to other Asian countries, as well as Europe and Africa, in the course of his professional life. He was a senior fellow of the prestigious Alexander von Humboldt Foundation in Germany. Mr. Nair also served as a professor at the University of Fort Hare, South Africa, the alma mater of President Nelson Mandela. It was Mr. Mandela who invited him to the country to set up a Department of Agriculture at the university.

After Mr. Nair presented a research paper on the concept of ‘nutrient buffer power’, explaining the principles governing the availability of nutrients in soil, at an international colloquium in France, he was appointed to the National Chair of the Science Foundation at The Royal Society of Belgium in 1984.

A prolific writer, he authored around 20 books, apart from regularly contributing to newspapers and magazines. Antonio Guterres, United Nations Secretary-General, launched his book on global warming in New York.
He is survived by his wife, Pankajam Nair, and two children.

articles.title: Congress, along with INDIA bloc partners, will present strong alternative to people in UP: Kharge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh will give a new direction to the country's politics, Mallikarjun Kharge said.

Amid the buzz over seat-sharing with the Samajwadi Party for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, the Congress' top leadership deliberated with the state leaders on Monday (November 16, 2026) with AICC chief Mallikarjun Kharge expressing confidence that his party, together with the INDIA bloc, will present a strong alternative to the people.

Besides Mr. Kharge, former Congress chief Rahul Gandhi, AICC general secretaries Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K.C. Venugopal, AICC in-charge of UP Rajendra Pal Gautam, UP Congress chief Aradhana Misra-Mona, UP Congress working president Imran Masood and Uttar Pradesh Congress Legislature Party leader Virendra Chaudhary attended the meeting at the party chief's 10, Rajaji Marg residence here.

In a post on X in Hindi after the meeting, Mr. Kharge said, "Today, I had an in-depth discussion with senior leaders of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee about the state's political situation and the upcoming assembly elections."
“The upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh will give a new direction to the country's politics,” Mr. Kharge said.

"The people of the state are looking for change and want to see social justice, equal opportunities and the rights of marginalised communities strengthened. I am fully confident that the Congress party, together with the INDIA alliance, will present a strong alternative to the people of Uttar Pradesh," Mr. Kharge said.

The Congress meeting comes just two days after Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav indicated on Saturday that the Congress has expressed its wish to contest 181 seats in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls.
Asked at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in Delhi whether the Congress is seeking to contest 100 seats, Yadav said the party has demanded more than that.

Asked if the demand was of 200 seats, he replied, "A little less than that." When the interviewer suggested 180 seats, Mr. Yadav said, "Add one more," indicating that the Congress has sought 181 seats from the SP.

"We have made up our mind on how many seats we will contest. The Samajwadi Party and the INDIA alliance will defeat the BJP together," he said, adding that the "theft" of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya will be a major poll issue.
Asked if he is considering an alliance with Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati, Yadav said he does not think of other alliances while being part of an existing one.

articles.title: Supreme Court rejects plea against Maharashtra's rotation policy for reserved SC/ST seats in local bodies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed an appeal filed by Sau. Rupali Indrabhushan Sonde against the September 19, 2025, judgment of the Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court, saying, "No voter or a candidate can have a vested right to have a constituency declared as a reserved seat for SCs or STs”

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) refused to entertain a plea challenging a provision in the Maharashtra government's rules that treats the general elections to Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis after the enforcement of the rules as the first for the rotation of reserved seats for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST).

A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed an appeal filed by Sau. Rupali Indrabhushan Sonde against the September 19, 2025, judgment of the Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court, saying, "No voter or a candidate can have a vested right to have a constituency declared as a reserved seat for SCs or STs."
The bench said such decisions fall under the policy domain, and the petitioner cannot say that the rotation policy has to be exercised in a particular manner.

The bench, however, took note of the submissions of senior advocate Vipin Sanghi, appearing for Sonde, and permitted the petitioner to file a representation to the Maharashtra government for reconsideration of the rules related to the reservation of seats for SCs and STs under the rotation policy for local body elections.

On September 19, 2025, a division bench comprising Justices Rajnish R. Vyas and Anil S. Kilor of the Bombay High Court dismissed a batch of petitions challenging the provision in the Maharashtra government's 2025 rules.

It had held that the petitioners failed to establish that the introduction of Rule XII of the Maharashtra Zilla Parishads and Panchayat Samitis (Manner and Rotation of Reservation of Seats) Rules, 2025, was arbitrary or unconstitutional.

"(XII) First Election for rotation: For rotation of seats under these Rules, the general election held after commencement of these Rules shall be considered as the first election," the impugned rule reads.

The plea challenged Rule XII, stating that the provision would disrupt the existing reservation rotation system and adversely affect candidates seeking to contest elections from reserved constituencies.

It was argued before the high court that the new rule was arbitrary, violated Article 14 of the Constitution and exceeded the scope of the parent Maharashtra Zilla Parishads and Panchayat Samitis Act, 1961.
The petitioners had also maintained that the right to contest elections would be affected by resetting the rotation process.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation surges to 12.29% in October, fuel and power prices lead rise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: According to provisional government data, inflation in the fuel and power category climbed to 32.84%, while primary articles recorded inflation of 9.24%. Inflation in manufactured products, meanwhile, eased marginally to 9.54%

India’s wholesale price inflation accelerated to 12.29% in October 2026, compared with 11.39% in September, according to provisional data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Monday. The All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for all commodities rose to 113.3 in October, from 112.5 in the previous month.

Fuel and power prices remained the biggest driver of wholesale inflation, with the category recording an annual inflation rate of 32.84% in October, sharply higher than the 25.85% recorded in September. Inflation in primary articles also increased to 9.24% from 8.67% during the same period. Meanwhile, inflation in manufactured products eased marginally to 9.54%, compared with 9.76% in September.

Within the fuel and power category, inflation in mineral oils rose to 45.57% in October from 40.02% in September. Crude petroleum and natural gas recorded a sharp increase, with inflation climbing to 70.80% from 57.32%. Electricity inflation also moved into positive territory at 8.06%, compared with -0.43% in the previous month.

The government’s data identified mineral oils, crude petroleum and natural gas, electricity, food articles, basic metals, chemicals, food products, non-food articles, textiles, and rubber and plastic products among the major contributors to wholesale price inflation during October.

The Wholesale Price Index’s food index, which accounts for 24.99% of the overall basket, recorded inflation of 8.58% in October, marginally lower than the 8.66% reported in September. Inflation in food articles under the primary articles category, however, rose to 8.26% from 8.14%.

Among manufactured products, inflation in chemicals and chemical products increased to 17.53% in October from 16.74% in September. Basic metals inflation rose to 17.21% from 16.96%, while textiles recorded inflation of 13.67%, compared with 13.85% in the previous month. Inflation in rubber and plastic products also increased to 13.90% from 13.47%.

The Ministry said the October WPI figures are provisional and have been compiled with a weighted response rate of 81.1%. The final WPI inflation rate for August 2026 remained unchanged at 9.92%, with the index at 110.8.
The government is scheduled to release the provisional Wholesale Price Index, Output Producer Price Index and trial Input Producer Price Index for November 2026 on December 14.

articles.title: Pakistan human rights body warns of escalating threats to democracy and fundamental freedoms
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: According to a press release issued by HRCP, the commission's General Body expressed alarm over the systematic erosion of freedom of expression through censorship, surveillance, restrictive regulations and the misuse of criminal laws

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP), following the conclusion of its 40th Annual General Meeting (AGM), has raised concerns over what it described as an escalating assault on constitutional democracy and fundamental rights across the country, warning that freedom of expression, judicial independence and democratic institutions are facing growing threats.

According to a press release issued by HRCP Chairperson Asad Iqbal Butt, the Commission's General Body expressed alarm over the systematic erosion of freedom of expression through censorship, surveillance, restrictive regulations and the misuse of criminal laws.

Highlighting the October 2026 sentencing of human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Chattha to ten years in prison, HRCP described the verdicts as a chilling example of how individuals exercising their constitutional rights could be targeted. The Commission also expressed concern over continued enforced disappearances and the detention of activists, including Mahrang Baloch, Ali Wazir and Idris Khattak. It called for all detainees to be produced before competent Courts, the repeal of arbitrary detention powers under the Anti-Terrorism Act and the abolition of internment centres.

HRCP further demanded the withdrawal of the proscription of the Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee in PoJK. Addressing the security situation in Balochistan, the General Body called for an open national debate on the province's challenges and urged the restoration of cross-border trade to safeguard local livelihoods.

The press release also highlighted concerns over what HRCP described as the erosion of federalism and democratic representation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It pointed to the imposition of an emergency and Governor's rule, the detention of the province's elected chief executive and the mass arrests of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf workers in October 2026. The Commission further criticised the Federal Constitutional Court's intervention restricting the Peshawar High Court's exercise of its constitutional jurisdiction, saying it undermined access to justice and judicial independence. It urged political parties to return to the democratic principles outlined in the Charter of Democracy rather than compromise institutional structures for political expediency.

On constitutional and judicial matters, HRCP said the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments had seriously weakened judicial independence and institutional checks and balances. It called for both amendments to be reviewed, lifetime immunity for public officeholders to be withdrawn and military trials of civilians to be brought to an end. The commission also stressed that any future constitutional amendments must be based on genuine cross-party political consensus. It said proposals to create new provinces should not undermine Pakistan's federal structure or come at the expense of strengthening local Governments.

Highlighting the situation of religious minorities, HRCP said targeted violence, discrimination and blasphemy-related persecution continued across the country. It pointed to attacks on Ahmadiyya places of worship, mob-led violence, including an attack against a Christian doctor in Sheikhupura, and the alleged entrapment of individuals in false blasphemy cases. The Commission called for the immediate constitution of the National Commission for Minorities and demanded accountability for individuals involved in inciting violence and orchestrating forced conversions.

On economic rights, HRCP warned that economic injustice was deepening, with austerity measures and inadequate social protection placing a disproportionate burden on low-income households. It called on the Government to prioritise living wages, decent employment opportunities and access to essential public services in its economic policies. The General Body also emphasised the State's responsibility to protect communities most vulnerable to violence and discrimination, particularly women, transgender persons and other marginalised groups, stressing that their fundamental rights must be ensured in practice rather than remain promises on paper.

Concluding its statement, HRCP reiterated the need to safeguard constitutional democracy, restore institutional independence and ensure accountability, warning that the continued erosion of fundamental freedoms and democratic structures poses serious challenges to the country's rights framework.

articles.title: Sudan Army strike kills 15, including children says rights group, survivor
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The double-tap strike on November 15 in the village of Abu Qalb also “injured others and burned a number of homes”, reported local rights monitor the Kordofan Observatory
A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people in a West Kordofan village including four children playing football, a survivor told AFP Monday (November 16, 2026).

The double-tap strike on Sunday (November 15, 2026) on the village of Abu Qalb also "injured others and burned a number of homes", reported local rights monitor the Kordofan Observatory, who gave the same toll.

The attack came as the Sudanese Army leads a counter-offensive through West Kordofan State to recapture territory from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), with whom it has been at war since April 2023.

"We lost 15 people. Two of the children had already lost their father earlier in the war, and nine of those killed were my own relatives," the survivor said, using a satellite internet connection to circumvent a communications blackout.
South Sudan postpones first national elections until February
UN peacekeepers failed to protect civilians before South Sudan massacre: Amnesty

Requesting anonymity for his safety, he said the drone struck the village twice. The first hit a public square, where the children were playing football, while the second hit local homes, setting several on fire.
The war has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and has triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.
The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026 alone.
Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes, the UN said this week.

articles.title: Ukraine hits Russia's Crimea bridge in 1,300-drone barrage
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The strike on the bridge appeared to inflict only minor damage, though drew an angry response from Russian-installed officials
Ukraine fired hundreds of drones at Russia overnight, aiming towards Moscow and hitting a symbolic bridge that links the annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia.
The strike on the bridge appeared to inflict only minor damage, though drew an angry response from Russian-installed officials.

Ukraine launched 1,336 drones in the barrage, Moscow's defence ministry said in a statement -- the second-highest daily figure so far this year, according to an AFP tally of official Russian statements.

The barrage came days before a summit in Shenzhen between President Vladimir Putin, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. U.S. officials say Russia's war against Ukraine is not expected to be a focus of the talks.
"The enemy has hit the Crimea bridge," the Crimean Russian-installed governor Sergey Aksyonov wrote on Telegram. "As a result, traffic will be restricted, likely until the afternoon."
He did not say whether anyone was killed or wounded in the strike. Social media channels close to the Russian army indicated no serious damage had been sustained in the attack.
The bridge has been a key target for Ukraine since Russia launched its offensive in February 2022.
It has been struck several times, including an October 2022 blast in which an explosive-packed truck was detonated on the bridge, causing months of disruption.
Around 600 of the drones were intercepted on approach to the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.

Ukraine fired hundreds of drones at Russia overnight, aiming towards Moscow and hitting a symbolic bridge that links the annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia.

The strike on the bridge appeared to inflict only minor damage, though drew an angry response from Russian-installed officials.

Ukraine launched 1,336 drones in the barrage, Moscow's defence ministry said in a statement -- the second-highest daily figure so far this year, according to an AFP tally of official Russian statements.

The barrage came days before a summit in Shenzhen between President Vladimir Putin, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. U.S. officials say Russia's war against Ukraine is not expected to be a focus of the talks.

"The enemy has hit the Crimea bridge," the Crimean Russian-installed governor Sergey Aksyonov wrote on Telegram. "As a result, traffic will be restricted, likely until the afternoon."

He did not say whether anyone was killed or wounded in the strike. Social media channels close to the Russian army indicated no serious damage had been sustained in the attack.

The bridge has been a key target for Ukraine since Russia launched its offensive in February 2022.

It has been struck several times, including an October 2022 blast in which an explosive-packed truck was detonated on the bridge, causing months of disruption.

Around 600 of the drones were intercepted on approach to the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.

The interceptions came hours after Ukrainian forces struck a major Russian petrochemical plant, an oil refinery and a military production site.

articles.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin summit in Shenzhen on November 19
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Chinese Foreign Ministry gave no further details including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be
China confirmed that President Xi Jinping and his U. S. and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday (November 19, 2026) in Shenzhen.

“On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen,” the Foreign Ministry said in a brief statement on Monday (November 16, 2026).
It gave no further details including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be.
It is expected to happen on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) and Thursday (November 19, 2026).
The Kremlin and the White House had both previously confirmed the three-way meeting.
Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said that in a recent meeting, Mr. Xi showed “irritation” when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up.
“He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Mr. Steinmeier told ARD.
On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the United States and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile.

China’s Foreign Ministry said on Monday (November 16, 2026) ​that this week’s trilateral meeting between ‌the Chinese, U.S. and Russian leaders ​is of “groundbreaking significance” and will ⁠promote world peace and stability.

articles.title: India, U.S., eight other nations sign declaration to safeguard AI supply chains
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Pax Silica initiative was announced by the U.S. in December last year to secure supply chains for silicon and other minerals essential to semiconductor production and, by extension, to AI

India, the U.S. and eight other countries have signed a declaration to treat safeguarding Artificial Intelligence (AI) supply chains as a “shared endeavour” amid growing competition with China in emerging technology.

The San Francisco Declaration was signed at a meeting of the founders of the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative convened by U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The declaration was released by the Governments of the U.S., Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom.

The Pax Silica initiative was announced by the U.S. in December last year to secure supply chains for silicon and other minerals essential to semiconductor production and, by extension, to artificial intelligence and other advanced technological industries.

The declaration on Sunday (November 15) affirms that economic security is fundamental to national security, sets out the participants’ common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure that underpin Super Intelligence supply chains, and declares that safeguarding them is a shared endeavour, a State Department statement said.
The U.S. government refers to Artificial Intelligence (AI) as Super Intelligence (SI) after President Donald Trump signed an executive order to rename it.
The Declaration on Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity also resolves to establish working groups to carry common purpose into common practice.

It proposed to set up five groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, SI adoption in key sectors, supply chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbours and supply chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience.
“No nation can secure the foundations of the SI era alone, and the prosperity SI makes possible will only be as durable as the supply chains and infrastructure beneath it,” the statement said.

The declaration said that by agreeing on what must be protected and committing to protect it together, participants are laying the secure foundations on which partner nations can innovate, invest, and grow.

fullParagraphs: Dhun Davar, deputy CEO & chief of programmes, AVPN spoke to The Hindu about the challenges in the TB elimination programme

India’s tuberculosis (TB) burden remains substantial despite progress. The country has the largest TB burden in the world, accounting for approximately one-quarter of all TB cases globally. The number of new cases fell 21% between 2015 and 2024, while treatment coverage rose to 92%, according to World Health Organisation data cited by the government. The Central government recently started the JOSH campaign -- launched in 11 States and 55 districts to promote screening, early diagnosis and treatment adherence. JOSH stands for Joint Squad for Health. It is a youth-led community mobilisation initiative to strengthen India’s campaign to eliminate TB.

Dhun Davar, deputy CEO & chief of programmes, AVPN, spoke to The Hindu about the challenges in the TB elimination programme. AVPN is a pan-Asian network of social investors, philanthropists, foundations, corporations and other organisations that work to direct funding and expertise towards social and environmental challenges. Its work includes health equity, gender equality, climate action and economic inclusion.

articles.title: 29th edition of Bengaluru Tech Summit to kick off on November 17
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will inaugurate the three-day event, themed: “AI & Beyond,” on Tuesday morning

Karnataka is set to host the 29th edition of its flagship annual technology exposition, the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS), from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC).
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will inaugurate the three-day event, themed: “AI & Beyond,” on Tuesday morning.

Addressing a media conference on the eve of the summit, Minister for Home, IT & BT, and e-Governance Priyank Kharge said that the conference would feature over 120 knowledge sessions across 16 thematic tracks, including IT & DeepTech, Frontier Tech, Electro-Semicon, Electric Mobility, Health & Biotech, Digital Infrastructure & Data Centres, Data & Cybersecurity, Assistive Tech, Focus GCC, Circular Economy, Orange Economy, Finverse, Skilling & Edutech, India–USA Tech Conclave, Global Collaborations, and India Innovates.

Highlighting the summit’s global trajectory, Mr. Kharge noted how the expo has expanded over the decades to draw international participation. “Bengaluru Tech Summit has evolved beyond an annual technology gathering into a platform where global conversations translate into partnerships, investments, and tangible opportunities,” the Minister said.
The State’s ambition was to make Bengaluru a gateway for the world to engage with India’s technology ecosystem, while taking Karnataka’s innovations and solutions to global markets, he added.

articles.title: DVAC registers criminal case over alleged irregularities in the purchase of books
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The criminal case has been registered against a Chennai-based publisher and “unidentified officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai, and Periyar Arivulagam, Coimbatore. On Monday (November 16, 2026), DVAC officials launched a search at seven places and seized receipt vouchers for book procurement and other documents. Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers, was arrested

The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a criminal case against a Chennai-based publisher and “unidentified officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai, and Periyar Arivulagam, Coimbatore, over allegations of large-scale irregularities in the procurement of books.

The case was registered after prima facie evidence pointing to forgery, criminal conspiracy, and corruption was established in a detailed inquiry conducted on a complaint filed by the Secretary, School Education Department, who sought a probe into the alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for public libraries.
Investigation revealed that the “coordination committee” had added titles not recommended by the “books recommendation committee”, which had proposed around 26,000 books for purchase.
These additions were not brought on record in the official note file, the First Information Report said.

It also revealed that books were allegedly written in fictitious names, with plagiarised content and violations of the Transparent Book Procurement Policy, 2024, which prescribed a systematic, transparent, and structured procedure for the purchase of books for public libraries.

Besides the officials, the agency booked R. Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers (also known as Akal Vilakku Pathippagam), and Phoenix Publications, both based at Madipakkam, Chennai, and other unidentified persons.

The DVAC said in its FIR that the State government had sanctioned ₹50 crore for procuring books and e-books for Periyar Arivulagam. The procurement was also intended to cover Kamarajar Arivulagam, Tiruchi; Bharathidasan Arivulagam, Salem; Anjalai Ammal Arivulagam, Cuddalore; Quaid-e-Millath Arivulagam, Tirunelveli; and libraries in six newly formed districts.

The agency said Mohan was the proprietor of both publishing firms that had operated from the same address and were associated with Sigma Prints and Sigma Publishing Services. He had given a list of 2,339 titles in the name of Akal Vizhakku Publishers and 99 titles in the name of Phoenix Publications. Purchase orders for 1,857 books were issued to the two publishers on February 13 and 14, 2026. After the books were received and verified, the list submitted by Akal Vizhakku Publishers was forwarded for processing payment for 1,779 books.

Investigators said Mohan had “created the books under fictitious author names, using information taken from websites and online applications, including ChatGPT. The contents were found to be vague, irrelevant and misleading, and of substandard language with no educational or informational value for a public library”.

The inquiry exposed instances of factually wrong information and plagiarism. One book described Naladiyar as a poet and philosopher, while another said the author of Madurai Kanchi was a king. The book titled Tourism: Principles, Practices and Philosophies, attributed to Emily Lawson, contained material copied from other books.

articles.title: Delhi car blast: SC allows transfer of cases to capital for joint trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed a plea by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) for transfer of two criminal cases linked to the November 2025 car explosion near the Red Fort Metro station from Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana to a special court in the national capital.
A Bench headed by Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra also directed that three FIRs registered in the matter across Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana be clubbed together for a joint trial in Delhi.
A powerful explosion ripped through a slow-moving car at a traffic signal near the Red Fort Metro station on November 10, 2025, killing 12 people and injuring several others.

The apex court pointed to the overlapping of accused persons, witnesses and evidence, making separate trials in different States unfeasible. The court also took into consideration the security of the trial, with several accused persons still absconding.

The NIA said the cases were linked through an interweaving of facts, like the proliferation of provocative and inflammatory posters associated with the proscribed terrorist organisation Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) in Srinagar, ahead of the blast.
All three cases were intricately connected and formed part of one overarching conspiracy, requiring a joint trial in one place.
Following the blast, several arrests were made, including that of four doctors. The alleged car bomber, Umar Nabi, was reported to be a doctor himself.
