articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: According to economists, not only will this high wholesale inflation soon translate into higher consumer prices, but it also means an interest rate hike is nearly certain, which would dampen economic sentiment

Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.

The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.

However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.

The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

fullParagraphs: Trump said Jensen Huang ‘learned a big lesson’ and he ‘would certainly not mind’ if he was reinstated, while adding that there’s a ‘big group of people that would like him to return’

Jensen Huang is reportedly trying to make a comeback as CEO of Nvidia as a campaign to reinstate him picked up steam Monday, with support from tech industry leaders as well as many of the chipmaker's employees.

U.S. President Donald Trump, who has been close with Mr. Huang, also suggested he could return to Nvidia. Mr. Trump said Mr. Huang “learned a big lesson” and he “would certainly not mind” if he was reinstated.
There’s a “big group of people that would like him to return,” Mr. Trump added.
SpaceX and Tesla boss Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, CEO of video game maker Epic Games, were among thousands of people who signed an online petition calling for Huang to return to the company.

Mr. Huang resigned last week from Nvidia, apparently ousted by the board after revelations that he had extramarital affairs, both with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing and with a senior executive who reported to him. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement.

Mr. Huang is plotting a comeback, the Financial Times reported over the weekend, citing multiple anonymous sources. The newspaper said he has been discussing the possibility with confidants, as his allies assembled a “war room” of Silicon Valley allies to lobby for his return.

The “Stand with Jensen” petition was set up Friday (November 13) and soon gathered momentum, gaining signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other supporters. It calls on the board to bring back Mr. Huang while an independent investigation proceeds or there's “compelling evidence” that his departure is in the company's best interests.

“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the petition's organizers said in an open letter. “We do not have access to the Board's private deliberations. We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy.”
The identities of the signatories could not be independently verified, and the website said that their “affiliations are self-reported and not verified.”
Some people posted on their personal accounts that they supported the effort.

articles.title: India and Egypt form working group to explore trade deal contours
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India and Egypt have agreed to establish a joint working group to explore the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement between the two countries, the government announced on Monday (November 16, 2026).

During his ongoing visit to Egypt, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal co-chaired, along with Egypt’s Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh, the 7th session of the India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital.
This was the first time this JTC has been convened at the ministerial level.

“As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries,” the government said in a release.
The release also said that both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of $12 billion.

“Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains,” the release said.
“India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships,” it added.

The committee also reviewed the growth in India-Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to $6.5 billion in 2025-26. Trade during the first half of the current financial year (April-September 2026) also stood at a little more than $5 billion, up 65% over its level in the same period of 2025.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts

Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye.

Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere. Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively.

The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan. The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement.

The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance. This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change.

Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways.

Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027. The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production. Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions.

Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035. Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency.

COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements. He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding. He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.

The U SS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the West Asia, once again bringing the total number of U.S. aircraft carriers in the West Asia to three — an unusually high number.
A U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations, on Monday (November 16, 2026) confirmed the carrier’s arrival in the region.
It brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as President Donald Trump has kept his options open during the more than 8-month-old Iran war.
The Roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September.

The Theodore Roosevelt joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as scores of smaller navy ships, that are in the region maintaining a blockade of Iranian shipping. The H.W. Bush arrived in the region in April while the George Washington arrived in August.
According to the Navy, the flotilla in the Arabian Sea now includes three aircraft carriers as well as 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship.

articles.title: After Yemen setback, Saudi Arabia replaces military commander
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group

Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis ‌on Monday (November 16, 2026) after Riyadh’s Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in ​a major setback for their campaign against the group.

The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group.

After gaining ground in a counter-attack in October, the Yemeni government said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) it was withdrawing from ‌areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery, to focus on defending its base of operations in Aden, a port city on the southern coast.

People in the Yemeni military ‌said on Monday (November 16, 2026) the Houthis had advanced to the southern coastal area of Khor Omairh, ‌some ⁠100 km (62 miles) west of Aden and were 25 km (16 miles) from government lines at Qawah, ⁠another coastal area.
A royal decree issued by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman spelt out changes to the command of the Saudi-led coalition.

The existing commander, Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman, was appointed as adviser to the defence minister for military affairs, while Chief of ​the General Staff General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili was assigned ‌the additional role of commanding the joint forces, Saudi state media reported.
Two Western diplomats linked the change directly to battlefield developments in Yemen and the Houthi advance.
The Saudi government media office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports and ‌oil facilities since the Yemen war restarted.
Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on ​Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have enhanced Iran’s position in the wider Middle East conflict.

articles.title: Israeli opposition chiefs denounce Netanyahu over ‘attempted coup’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats

Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday (November 16, 2026) an "attempted coup" following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.

"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list.

Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday (November 15, 2026) that on the eve of the October 27 election, Mr. Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.
Mr. Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source -- a former employee of Mr. Netanyahu's office -- who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.
The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.
Mr. Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.
Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu".

"If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.
Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.

articles.title: AIIMS Delhi performs a life-changing spinal repair in utero, before the patient’s first breath
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: This is India’s first open foetal repair for myelomeningocele, a defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine; over 30 clinicians and nurses involved in multidisciplinary procedure

The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi has performed India’s first open foetal repair of a lumbosacral myelomeningocele — the most severe form of spina bifida — at 25 weeks’ gestation.

“The six-hour operation repaired the cerebrospinal-fluid-leaking lumbosacral defect in utero. It followed more than five weeks of multidisciplinary planning, detailed foetal imaging, non-directive counselling, anaesthetic preparation, and operative simulation,’’ AIIMS said in a statement.
A myelomeningocele is an open neural tube defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine.

The patient was first screened and counselled by K. Aparna Sharma from the Maternal–Fetal Medicine team. The multidisciplinary procedure was performed using high-end microscopy and continuous high-end ultrasonography assistance at the Neurosciences Centre. The procedure was provided free of cost to the family under the Union government’s Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK).

Deepak Gupta, who led the neurosurgical component, said that the intervention was done after rigorous selection. “Prenatal repair seeks to limit ongoing injury to exposed neural tissue, reduce the subsequent need for cerebrospinal-fluid diversion for hydrocephalus, and improve selected neurological outcomes. It is not a cure, and long-term multidisciplinary care remains essential,” he said.

More than 30 clinicians and nurses from the Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Maternal–Fetal Medicine, Neurosurgery, Obstetrics and Neuroanaesthesia, Plastic Surgery, Radiodiagnosis, Neonatology, and Nursing teams of the Neurosciences Centre and Obstetrics–Gynaecology services participated in the procedure.

Professor Aparna Sharma added that this foetal intervention was well-reasoned and a planned decision aimed to optimise the outcomes of both the baby and the mother. The safety of both mother and foetus was ensured through detailed counselling, high-quality anaesthesia, and coordinated surveillance before and after surgery.

“International trial evidence supports prenatal repair in carefully selected foetuses with open myelomeningocele. The procedure nevertheless carries important maternal and foetal risks, including prematurity and uterine-scar complications, and must be performed only in specialised centres,’’ she said.

The team emphasised that foetal surgery is a treatment for selected pregnancies, not a substitute for prevention. Neural-tube closure occurs by approximately 28 days after conception, often before pregnancy is recognised. Pre-conception folic-acid counselling, evidence-based food fortification with folates, and robust national surveillance remain essential to reducing India’s burden of neural tube defects.

“The mother and foetus will continue to receive close multidisciplinary surveillance through pregnancy, delivery, and the newborn period,’’ the AIIMS statement said, adding that a child with spina bifida may begin life with paralysis, hydrocephalus, and lifelong challenges.

articles.title: 29-year-old regains limb movement after emergency stroke treatment at two govt. hospitals
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A 29-year-old woman from Manuguru, who was rushed to hospital after suddenly losing movement in her right arm and leg, regained significant mobility within hours after doctors at two government hospitals coordinated to administer emergency stroke treatment within the critical window.

Rajani’s ordeal began on an ordinary morning when she suddenly developed slurred speech and complete weakness on her right side. Recognising the signs of an acute stroke, doctors acted swiftly to prevent permanent brain damage.

She was first taken to Area Hospital, Manuguru, where Sai Kumar, a General Medicine specialist, identified the symptoms and arranged an urgent referral to Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, nearly 60 km away, for emergency treatment.

Recognising the narrow window for intervention, M. Ramakrishna, medical superintendent of Area Hospital, Manuguru, coordinated directly with Tejaswi Gadde, physician at Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, to facilitate her transfer.

At Bhadrachalam, doctors immediately conducted a CT scan to rule out bleeding in the brain before administering clot-dissolving medication. With Rajani still within the recommended 4.5-hour treatment window, doctors administered intravenous Tenecteplase at 2 p.m., around 3.5 hours after the symptoms began, said G. Ravi Babu, District Coordinator of Hospital Services (DCHS), Bhadradri Kothagudem.

The response to treatment was encouraging. Before the intervention, Rajani had no detectable movement in her right arm or leg, with her muscle power recorded at 0/5. Following thrombolysis, her muscle strength improved, and she regained the ability to move the affected limbs against resistance, though full strength is yet to return.

She remains under close neurological observation. The case also highlights the availability of advanced emergency treatment in government hospitals serving remote and tribal areas. The thrombolytic medication, which costs around ₹45,000 in the market, was administered to Rajani free of cost.

Dr. Ravi Babu appreciated the doctors, nurses and supporting staff at both hospitals for their prompt decisions and coordination. “Such interventions demonstrate how teamwork between government healthcare institutions can help deliver advanced, life-saving treatment even in geographically remote areas,” he said.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.

Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.

The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.

Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”

Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.

For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.

The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.

articles.title: Pollution in Yamuna increased despite huge expenditure on cleaning: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: “This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna,” said SC

Pollution in Yamuna has only increased despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, the Supreme Court has said, directing the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to monitor water quality at the points where the Yamuna and its major drains enter and exit states, Union territories and districts.

In an order dated November 4, a Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan observed that industrial pollutants and untreated sewage must be stopped at the source, and merely constructing more sewage treatment plants is not sufficient to clean the river.

"This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna. This is why, despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, pollution in the Yamuna has only increased," the Bench said while hearing a plea related to cleaning of the river.
The top court said industrial pollution and untreated sewage must be curtailed, if not stopped altogether, at the source.

"Where that is not possible, the sewage must first be tapped and then treated. However, tapping will remain a challenge in absence of a robust sewage system and due to joining of stormwater and sewage drains.

"This court is further of the opinion that it would be difficult, if not impossible, for civic authorities to tap sewage in most illegal and unauthorised colonies built on encroached land, since they have not been built on a grid layout and have hardly any space for laying a sewage system," it said.

The apex court said unless illegal and unauthorised colonies and 'jhuggi-jhopdi' (slum) clusters on the drains as well as on the river bed are removed, with rehabilitation of their occupants, their sewage will continue to pollute the river.
The court directed that if water quality deteriorates while passing through a particular state, Union territory or district, the concerned authorities would be held accountable and penalised.

"If the water quality deteriorates on any parameter while flowing through, or exiting a state/Union territory or a district therein, that state/Union territory or district... shall be held accountable and penalised. The said compensation/ fine shall be deposited with the registry of this court," the Bench said, directing CPCB to suggest a formula for calculating the said compensation.

articles.title: India scrutinises Red Bull’s sugar levels as ‘energy drink’ dispute escalates
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation, the FSSAI said in the document

India is scrutinising the composition of Red Bull, the drink made by the eponymous Austrian company, warning the product’s “energy drink” label could encourage people to consume too much added sugar, an official notice showed, opening a new front in the regulator’s fight over food safety standards.

It is the first time India has raised health concerns and questioned companies on the ingredients of their energy drinks in a dispute that began in June and has triggered legal challenges in the Delhi High Court.

In a confidential notice to Red Bull on Monday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) targeted the drink’s “nutritional composition”, saying it derived a significant proportion of its declared energy from the “substantial” amount of added sugar.
“The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation,” the FSSAI said in the document, which was reviewed by Reuters.

The notice gives Red Bull seven days to explain why India should not prohibit its use of the “energy drink” label given it had the “potential to mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption of added sugar.”
Red Bull and the FSSAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

India’s energy drinks market is set to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, with sales growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China, according to Euromonitor. Red Bull’s India revenue stood at $130 million in 2024, more than double the earnings recorded four years ago.

Health experts are concerned energy drinks contain high levels of sugar, caffeine and taurine, an amino acid that research suggests can contribute to health problems. The drinks will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year.

In court in recent weeks, Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer have challenged the June order banning the label “energy drinks”, saying they were not given any advance notice of the strict action.

However, while Red Bull managed to secure a temporary court injunction to enable it to continue using the “energy drink” label, its competitors were told that once they sold their existing stock they had to stop using the label.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 15 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. ✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 15 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Caste and class: On OBC reservation

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: IChE-HRC organises Dr. H. L. Roy memorial seminar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian Institute of Chemical Engineers – Hyderabad Regional Centre (IIChE-HRC) organised Dr. H. L. Roy memorial seminar on Saturday in the Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC) on the theme - Innovations in Green Technologies & Sustainable Manufacturing: Shaping the Future of Chemical Engineering.
The seminar commemorated Dr. Hira Lal Roy, the founding father of chemical engineering education and research in India, who established IIChE in 1947.

The inaugural session commenced with a welcome address by M. Misra, chairman, IIChE-HRC, who highlighted the significance of the seminar theme and the role of chemical engineers in promoting sustainable industrial development.

Dr. Komal Kapoor, Chairman & Chief Executive, NFC, emphasised the importance of technological innovation, operational excellence and sustainable practices in the nuclear sector. He elaborated the role of chemical engineer from ore to core and importance in reprocessing.

M. Narayana Reddy, Managing Director (Technical), Virchow Laboratories Limited, highlighted the need for industry–academia collaboration, adoption of green technologies and development of sustainable manufacturing practices to address emerging industrial challenges.

The technical sessions featured six eminent speakers representing premier research, academic and industrial organisations, who included Dr. S. K. Satpati, OS & Head, UED, MG/BARC, DAE; Shri Darshan B. Sathe, Executive Director, Fuel Fabrication, INRP(O), NRB, BARC; Prof. Dr. Chandra Shekhar Sharma, Head, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Hyderabad; Dr. S. Sridhar, Chief Scientist & Chair (CE & PT), CSIR-IICT; Shri Mahimabrata Misra, General Manager, NFC; and Dr. Venkata Nori, Co-Founder & CEO, AltNxt Energy Pvt. Ltd.
The event witnessed the participation of 120 delegates.
The seminar reinforced the vital role of chemical engineers in advancing clean energy, resource efficiency, technological innovation and sustainable industrial development, informed a press release.

articles.title: AIADMK to protest seeking action against Deputy Speaker in Thuraiyur ‘assault’ incident
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Edappadi K. Palaniswami criticises Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for remaining silent on the issue

The AIADMK has announced a protest on November 18, demanding action over an alleged incident in which M. Ravisankar, the TVK MLA for Thuraiyur and Deputy Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assaulted a social activist.

In a statement, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami alleged that Karthik Kumar, a social activist who went to meet Mr. Ravisankar to submit grievances, was subjected to a “brutal attack” and “verbal abuse”.

Mr. Palaniswami further claimed that after evidence of the assault surfaced, Mr. Ravisankar threatened the activist again and used a police officer to coerce the victim into posting on social media that the incident had never occurred. He remarked that this demonstrated how brazenly TVK legislators were engaging in hooliganism, which surpassed even what was depicted in films.

Criticising Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for remaining silent on the issue, Mr. Palaniswami announced that the AIADMK would stage a condemnation protest at 10 a.m. on Wednesday (November 18 near the Anna Statue at the Thuraiyur bus stand, demanding strict action against Mr. Ravisankar.

articles.title: NCP merger talks ended with death of Ajit Pawar, says Supriya Sule
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Date was set for merger of two NCP factions, but talks ended the day the former Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister died, says his cousin Supriya Sule

Putting a “full stop” on the discussion of a potential merger between the two Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) factions, NCP(Sharad Pawar) MP Supriya Sule said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that the talks ended with the death of her cousin Ajit Pawar , the former national president of the rival faction.

“The merger talks were on till my brother was alive and the date was set. The day he died, the talks were given a full stop. Our spokesperson never made statements on it or gave counters to rival faction,” Ms. Sule told the media.
Ajit Pawar, the former Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra, died in an aircraft accident on January 28 at Baramati airport in Pune.

The speculation of a possible reunion between the rival factions have been intensifying over the last few days amid several high-profile meetings, including between senior NCP working president Praful Patel and NCP(SP) supremo Sharad Pawar. Meanwhile, current Deputy Chief Minister and NCP national president Sunetra Pawar met Chief Minister and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday.

NCP MP Sunil Tatkare dismissed any political intention behind Mr. Patel’s meeting with Mr. Sharad Pawar and called it a personal visit. The buzz of merger had intensified after senior NCP leaders met Union Home Minister Amit Shah and it gained further momentum ahead of Mr. Shah’s scheduled visit to Pune on Sunday (November 15).

Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut advised NCP(SP) not to get swept away in the merger game for ministerial posts, saying “there may be a handful of people in Sharad Pawar’s party desperate for ministerial posts but it is not right for Sharad Pawar to destroy the principles he has upheld throughout his life for their sake.”

The leader of the NCP(SP)’s Opposition ally also highlighted that it does not suit the faction to discuss matters with a group that “licks the BJP’s boots” and create an “atmosphere of confusion” in Maharashtra.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi promises social security, insurance cover for gig workers in Telangana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr Gandhi said every gig worker would receive ₹5 lakh in accident insurance and ₹10 lakh in health insurance. A social security contribution mechanism under which 1% of every transaction, including deliveries and cab rides, would be contributed towards the workers’ future security

articles.title: CM promises govt. support to India’s newest public health university coming up in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy assured the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) of the State government’s full support for establishing its Institute of Public Health Sciences (IPHS) Deemed-to-be University in Hyderabad, setting June 2, 2028, as the deadline for completing the proposed campus and promising assistance with land, funds, permissions and other requirements.

Speaking at the foundation-laying ceremony and unveiling of the campus master plan on Saturday, Mr. Reddy said the government was committed to developing the institution into a world-class university that would contribute to public health education, research and healthcare in India and internationally.

He further added that the proposed university was not merely another educational institution but a project of global significance. Expressing confidence in its potential, he said he hoped that in the coming years, people would discuss the PHFI university alongside established institutions such as Harvard and Oxford.

The Chief Minister recalled how institutions such as the Indian School of Business (ISB) had contributed to Hyderabad’s emergence as an educational and knowledge hub. He said individuals who had established successful institutions had helped create a distinct identity for the city and that the PHFI university would add to this legacy.
PHFI Chairman Rajat Gupta said the university aspired to achieve excellence through world-class faculty, students, international collaborations and infrastructure.

PHFI IPHS Chancellor Dr. K. Srinath Reddy said PHFI aspired to become the world’s leading public health institution with the establishment of the university in Hyderabad. Dr. Reddy said the foundation’s work involved advancing multidisciplinary education and research through multi-sectoral implementation and multi-stakeholder engagement. The objective was to improve life expectancy, strengthen health systems, align policies across sectors with population health goals and encourage active community engagement.

Pro-Chancellor Sanjay Zodpey said the university was being conceived as a long-term institution that would serve generations of students, researchers, public health professionals and communities. He said the public health challenges of the 21st century required professionals with interdisciplinary perspectives, evidence-based knowledge and a commitment to equity and social impact.

Vice-Chancellor M. Vishnu Vardhana Rao outlined the university’s academic journey and expansion plans. The Indian Institute of Public Health Hyderabad was established in 2008 under the aegis of PHFI, with the objective of advancing public health through education, research and community engagement. The institution received recognition as a deemed-to-be university from the University Grants Commission in 2025, with Hyderabad as its main campus and Bengaluru as another campus, he said.

With the proposed campus and modern infrastructure, the institution plans to expand its academic offerings to at least six postgraduate programmes, two undergraduate programmes, PhD programmes and institute-level Master of Public Health programmes. It aims to build an academic community of approximately 2,500 students and research scholars over the next five years.

Dr. Rao said the university’s research priorities would include infectious diseases and pandemic preparedness, non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, One Health, mental health and disability. Digital health, artificial intelligence and data science would serve as cross-cutting areas across its research activities, he added.

articles.title: TGPCB recommends closures, forfeitures over dusty construction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) has received several complaints regarding air pollution caused by dust emissions from construction projects in the Tellapur and Kollur areas of Sangareddy district. After receiving several complaints of air pollution due to construction, the Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) constituted Rolling Task Force Teams to these projects and assess compliance with environmental regulations and implementation of air pollution control measures.

The team embarked on inspections and observed dust emissions from construction activity was aggravating air pollution. Several violations of environmental norms were also identified, the TGPCB stated.

The Committee reviewed the environmental compliance of as many as 16 construction projects. After examining the severity of the violations, committee recommended the issuing of closure orders against projects where serious violations were identified, along with the forfeiture of bank guarantees. The committee also recommended forfeiture of bank guarantees in respect of projects where minor violations were observed. A period of 10 days was recommended for the concerned projects to rectify the violations.

Three construction projects began construction activity without obtaining Consent for Establishment (CFE) from the Pollution Control Board, the TGPCB stated. The committee recommended the issuance of closure orders against these projects, it added. Two others were continuing construction activities in violation of the Orders for Suspension of Operations previously issued by the TGPCB, without obtaining permission from the Board for revocation of the suspension orders.

The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) has received several complaints regarding air pollution caused by dust emissions from construction projects in the Tellapur and Kollur areas of Sangareddy district. After receiving several complaints of air pollution due to construction, the Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) constituted Rolling Task Force Teams to these projects and assess compliance with environmental regulations and implementation of air pollution control measures.

The team embarked on inspections and observed dust emissions from construction activity was aggravating air pollution. Several violations of environmental norms were also identified, the TGPCB stated.

The Committee reviewed the environmental compliance of as many as 16 construction projects. After examining the severity of the violations, committee recommended the issuing of closure orders against projects where serious violations were identified, along with the forfeiture of bank guarantees. The committee also recommended forfeiture of bank guarantees in respect of projects where minor violations were observed. A period of 10 days was recommended for the concerned projects to rectify the violations.

Three construction projects began construction activity without obtaining Consent for Establishment (CFE) from the Pollution Control Board, the TGPCB stated. The committee recommended the issuance of closure orders against these projects, it added. Two others were continuing construction activities in violation of the Orders for Suspension of Operations previously issued by the TGPCB, without obtaining permission from the Board for revocation of the suspension orders.

A Ready Mix Concrete plant operating in association with another construction project was found to be functioning without obtaining Consent for Operation (CFO) from the TGPCB. The plant was also found to be lacking adequate air pollution control measures, thereby contributing to air pollution in the surrounding areas. The Task Force Committee recommended closure of the operations of this RMC plant as well.

articles.title: Six-month traffic disruption ahead as Ranigunj railway underpass work to begin in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The existing 13-metre carriageway will be widened to 22 metres, allowing four-way traffic movement, with an additional three metres of road space sought at Karbala Maidan to facilitate one-way movement during diversions.

For motorists navigating the Ranigunj rail underpass during peak hours, the familiar sight is a long queue of vehicles inching towards the narrow passage from Tank Bund, with buses, trucks, cars and two-wheelers jostling for space. What should be a short passage into a frustrating bottleneck. The proposed widening promises relief, but commuters will have to negotiate six months of traffic diversions before the work is completed.

Work on widening the Ranigunj Road Under Bridge (RuB) is expected to begin within a week. The existing carriageway, which is around 13 metres wide and currently accommodates two-way traffic, will be expanded to 22 metres to facilitate four-way movement. Officials expect the additional width to ease congestion and improve traffic flow along the busy stretch.

Traffic will be diverted through alternative routes. Under the proposed plan, vehicles travelling from MG Road towards Paradise and Ranigunj will be asked to take a left towards Distillery Road, pass through another road underbridge and proceed towards Karbala before joining MG Road.

Buses and trucks will be diverted from Old Ambedkar towards Liberty, Kavadiguda and Musheerabad, while smaller vehicles will be routed through Karbala and Ranigunj. To facilitate smoother movement at Karbala, the concerned agency has been asked to provide an additional three metres of road space to enable one-way traffic.

Officials said that if congestion builds up near Karbala Maidan, a portion of the traffic will be diverted through Minister Road and Rasoolpura. Flexi boards and signboards have been put up along the stretch to alert motorists about the upcoming work and diversions.

Hyderabad, Telangana, 14/11/2026: A view of Ranigunj railway underpass near James Street railway station as part of the six-month traffic disruption ahead as underpass work to begin, in Secunderabad on Saturday, November 14, 2026. Photo: RAMAKRISHNA G/The Hindu | Photo Credit: RAMAKRISHNA G

A. Chandra Shekar, who works at the Nampally court, commutes every day from Bolarum to reach work by 9 a.m., travelling through the stretch during the morning rush hour. He said the diversions would mean a longer commute for the next six months, but felt the eventual improvement would justify the inconvenience. “Although it will be a struggle to make the extra ride to dodge the stretch for six months, I speak for everyone when I say that this will bring much relief to a lot of commuters,” he said.

For Kalpana C, the congestion is not restricted to peak hours. She travels along Hussain Sagar Road from Himayatnagar towards her home in Rasoolpura and said the stretch frequently gets choked. “I take the Hussain Sagar Road to come home in Rasoolpura from Himayatnagar and it chokes up at any given time. Check the maps and it will be red constantly, especially the road towards Paradise from Tank Bund,” she said.

An official traffic advisory detailing the vehicle-wise diversion routes and restrictions will be issued by the Hyderabad Traffic Police before construction begins. Commuters will be advised to follow the notified routes and plan their journeys accordingly.

articles.title: Traffic diversions for steel flyover construction in Banjara Hills

fullParagraphs: Traffic restrictions and diversions will be implemented on stretches between Srinagar Colony T-Junction and NTR Bhavan on Road No. 2, Banjara Hills, in view of the ongoing construction of a steel flyover between Jubilee Hills Check Post and NFCL under the H-CITI project.

According to the traffic advisory issued on Saturday, vehicles travelling from Srinagar Colony towards SNT Junction near the TV9 office and Road No. 2, Banjara Hills, will not be allowed to take a right turn at SNT Junction. Commuters will have to take a left turn and make a U-turn at NFCL to reach Road No. 2.

Vehicles coming from Begumpet towards SNT, Sagar Society, KBR Park entrance, Jubilee Hills Check Post, Road Nos. 36 and 45, and the Durgam Cheruvu Cable Bridge will have to take the Panjagutta Flyover ‘Y’ Junction towards Taj Krishna and Road No. 1, Banjara Hills. They should then take a right turn at the 1/10 Banjara Hills Junction towards Zaheranagar, Basavatarakam Cancer Hospital and Agarasen Island to reach their destinations.

Commuters travelling from Srinagar Colony towards NTR Bhavan and the Cable Bridge have been advised to proceed through Indiranagar Gadda, Venkatagiri and Jubilee Hills Road Nos. 10 and 36 towards Madhapur.

Vehicles coming from NFCL towards NTR Bhavan, Jubilee Hills Road Nos. 45 and 36, and Madhapur should take a right turn at Sagar Society ‘T’ Junction and proceed through Indiranagar Gadda, Srinagar Colony Main Road, Road No. 5, Venkatagiri Junction and Jubilee Hills Road Nos. 10 and 36.

The traffic police have advised commuters to avoid peak-hour travel between 8.30 a.m. and 11 a.m. and 5 p.m. and 9 p.m., wherever possible. They have also asked motorists to follow traffic police instructions and road signage, use navigation applications for updates, and prefer public transport and carpooling.
Commuters can contact the traffic helpline on 9010203626 for travel assistance. Traffic updates will also be available on the Hyderabad Traffic Police social media platforms.

articles.title: Telangana Greyhounds get new shooting range at Rajendranagar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Director General of Police C.V. Anand on Saturday inaugurated the SPS OODA Shoot House at the Telangana Greyhounds facility in Rajendranagar, with the unit asked to maintain its strength at no less than 700 personnel, and continue rigorous operational training.

The new facility has been named after martyrs Sandeep, Pavan and Sridhar. The OODA concept, which stands for Observe, Orient, Decide and Act, has been incorporated into its training approach to help commandos assess situations, make decisions and respond quickly.

Speaking at the event, Mr. Anand described the Telangana Greyhounds as a model for police forces across the country and said the unit, along with OCTOPUS, played an important role in addressing threats such as Naxalism, terrorism and hijackings. He recalled the role played by the Greyhounds in tackling Naxalite activities and terrorist threats during the 1980s.

The DGP called for continuous training in jungle warfare and operations in rugged, hilly terrain, and asked personnel to remain prepared to respond to emergencies, including hijackings and terrorist attacks. He also urged the team to secure first place in the All India Police Commando Competition scheduled to begin in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, on February 2, 2027. The Telangana Greyhounds secured fourth place in the competition held two years ago.

Mr. Anand also referred to the unit’s parade during the National Unity Day celebrations at Kevadia in Gujarat on October 31, which received appreciation. He commended personnel who had excelled in training and marksmanship.

Anil Kumar, Director General of Police (Operations) and head of the Greyhounds and OCTOPUS units, said special measures were being taken to improve personnel’s physical fitness, operational briefing skills and firing capabilities. Several senior police officers and Greyhounds personnel attended the inauguration.

articles.title: Eight varieties of pharmaceutical ingredients worth ₹3.54 lakh seized in TG SAFE raid at Ameenpur firm
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district.

The raid was conducted at Neocell Biotechnologies Private Limited, located at the Medical Devices Park in Sultanpur, on Friday, following credible information about the illegal stocking of pharmaceutical ingredients for sale without a valid drug licence.

According to TG SAFE, officials found eight varieties of APIs illegally stocked at the premises and seized drug stocks worth ₹3.54 lakh. Further investigation is under way, and action will be initiated against those responsible in accordance with the law, TG SAFE said.

They further added that stocking APIs for sale without a valid drug licence is punishable under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, with imprisonment of up to five years. TG SAFE’s Drugs Wing is responsible for issuing licences for the stocking and sale of APIs under the Act.

articles.title: Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Drought has devastated Maharashtra’s Beed district, pushing women farmers and labourers towards distress migration. Despite repeated pleas for employment, villagers say government job guarantees have failed them, even as the State announces a ₹6,728-crore package

The cotton plants are green, but the bolls are missing. Across the Chauhan family’s four-acre field in Majalgaon in Maharashtra’s Beed district, the plants stand stunted, their promise of a harvest withered by the absence of rain. What should have been a season of cotton picking has become a search for the few bolls the drought has spared.

Under the relentless October sun, Vanita Chauhan bends over the plants, picking the little cotton she can find. A tattered towel covers her head, shielding her from the scorching heat. Her full-sleeved shirt is buttoned up to her neck, while the red pallu of her sari is tied around her arm and neck, fashioned into an improvised pouch. She drops each cotton boll into it before moving hurriedly to the next plant.

articles.title: Maritime security in focus at India-Belgium naval talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The bilateral talk was aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation and further deepening navy-to-navy engagements between the two countries

Commander of the Belgian Navy, Rear Admiral Tanguy Botman, held talks with Indian Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan on a range of issues, including maritime security, operational engagements, and collaboration in naval technology, officials said on Saturday (November 15, 2026).
The bilateral talk was aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation and further deepening navy-to-navy engagements between the two countries.
On arrival, he paid homage to fallen soldiers by laying a wreath at the National War Memorial. Thereafter, he was accorded a ceremonial guard of honour at the South Block lawns.
He also interacted with other senior officials to explore avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation. India and Belgium share longstanding maritime linkages.

The visit marks an important milestone in bilateral navy-to-navy relations and is expected to provide impetus to maritime cooperation through strengthening existing engagements and exploration of new avenues for collaboration, the official said.
