articles.title: Villagers in 25 districts cast votes for panchayat elections’ final phase in Rajasthan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The final phase polls across 25 districts for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti faced EVM glitches, boycotts, and a 72% turnout

Villagers in 25 districts of Rajasthan cast their votes for the fourth and final phase of polling on Saturday to elect the Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti members at a total of 2,524 seats. An estimated 72% turnout of voters at 11,905 polling stations was recorded by the end of the day.

The polling for first, second and third phases of Panchayati Raj elections was held on October 22, October 28 and November 3, respectively. Counting of votes for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections across all four phases will be held on November 20, followed by elections for Zila Pramukhs and Panchayat Samiti Pradhans.

There were delays in polling at several places due to glitches in electronic voting machines (EVMs), while the voters at some villages in Baran and Jaisalmer districts boycotted the polling to press for their demands.

The villagers at Mundakya and Mundki in Baran boycotted the voting in protest against an irrigation project adversely affecting their lands. They have been demanding fair compensation for land acquisition for the project. The villagers at Bhojraj Ki Dhani in Jaisalmer did not cast their votes in protest against alleged anomalies in the reservation for Other Backward Classes.

Police took two persons into custody at a polling station in Sikar district’s Hapas village when they created a commotion while insisting on carrying their mobile phones inside the booth. The situation escalated when they began arguing with the polling officials and the policemen, leading to their detention on charges of disturbing peace.

The highest polling at 77% was reported at Baseri in Dholpur district. A total of 8,843 candidates are contesting 2,524 seats in the fourth phase, including 382 Zila Parishad wards and 2,142 Panchayat Samiti wards. There are 1,322 contestants for Zila Parishad seats and 7,521 for Panchayat Samiti wards.

Bharatiya Janata Party leader and former Minister Rajendra Rathore’s son Parakram Singh and daughter-in-law, Kanika, are among the prominent candidates contesting for Zila Parishad seats from Churu district.

The final phase of polling covered Balotra, Baran, Banswara, Beawar, Bharatpur, Bikaner, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Churu, Deeg, Didwana-Kuchaman, Dholpur, Hanumangarh, Jalore, Jaipur, Jhunjhunu, Jaisalmer, Karauli, Khairthal-Tijara, Pratapgarh, Sawai Madhopur, Salumber, Sikar, Sriganganagar and Tonk districts.

articles.title: Bomb rips through Damascus suburb; killing 2, including child
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The explosion took place in the southern Damascus suburb of Jaramana near a factory where batteries are produced, state TV said

An explosive device placed inside a car in a suburb of Syria’s capital exploded on Saturday evening (November 15, 2026), killing two people and wounding at least one, state TV and the Interior Ministry said.

The explosion took place in the southern Damascus suburb of Jaramana near a factory where batteries are produced, state TV said. It said two people were killed and two were wounded, without giving further details.
The Interior Ministry said the dead included a child, adding that one person was wounded. It said security forces cordoned off the area and started an investigation.

Several explosions have taken place in Damascus and its suburbs in recent months as the country’s security remains fragile nearly two years after five decades of Assad family rule ended in December 2024. Militants stormed the capital and removed then-President Bashar Assad from power.

Jaramana is home to a large community of the Druze religious minority. The suburb has faced tensions between some members of the community and Sunni Muslim Syrians supportive of the country’s current Islamist-led government.

articles.title: U.S. must respect India’s right to defend itself, maintain zero tolerance towards terrorism: Blinken
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “India is a global force,” Mr. Blinken said, adding that the relationship and shared interests between Washington and New Delhi were “really global in nature”

The U.S. must respect India's right to defend itself and should maintain a zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism, former U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken said on Saturday (November 14, 2026), while describing Washington’s ties with New Delhi and Islamabad as “fundamentally different".
“India is a global force,” Mr. Blinken said, adding that the relationship and shared interests between Washington and New Delhi were “really global in nature”.
In contrast, the U.S. relationship with Pakistan is “regional," he said during a conversation with Jawed Ashraf, chairman of the India Trade Promotion Organisation, at a summit in New Delhi.

“ The relations with Pakistan are regional, and there are still going to be important areas where we need to do things with them, particularly, for example, when it comes to counter-terrorism, but these are fundamentally different relationships,” he said.
“We have to have a zero-tolerance policy for terrorism. Period. And that means that we have to have respect for India's right to defend itself,” he added.

Mr. Blinken said the U.S. approach must include support for India’s efforts to respond to attacks as well as diplomatic efforts to prevent an escalation between New Delhi and Islamabad, the two nuclear-armed neighbours.
He added that efforts to prevent escalation were important given the destructive potential of the weapons both countries possess.

Reflecting on Washington's past engagement with Islamabad, Mr. Blinken said U.S. strategic interests during the Cold War and the war in Afghanistan may have led successive administrations to be less critical of Pakistan's civil-military establishment.
“And there's certainly an opportunity for the United States to do more,” he added.

On India-U.S. relations, Mr. Blinken described the transformation in ties over the past few decades as a shift from estrangement to a strategic partnership, underpinned by shared interests and people-to-people connections.

“India is a global force,” Mr. Blinken said, adding that the relationship and shared interests between Washington and New Delhi were “really global in nature”.

In contrast, the U.S. relationship with Pakistan is “regional," he said during a conversation with Jawed Ashraf, chairman of the India Trade Promotion Organisation, at a summit in New Delhi.

“ The relations with Pakistan are regional, and there are still going to be important areas where we need to do things with them, particularly, for example, when it comes to counter-terrorism, but these are fundamentally different relationships,” he said.

“We have to have a zero-tolerance policy for terrorism. Period. And that means that we have to have respect for India's right to defend itself,” he added.

Mr. Blinken said the U.S. approach must include support for India’s efforts to respond to attacks as well as diplomatic efforts to prevent an escalation between New Delhi and Islamabad, the two nuclear-armed neighbours.

He added that efforts to prevent escalation were important given the destructive potential of the weapons both countries possess.

Reflecting on Washington's past engagement with Islamabad, Mr. Blinken said U.S. strategic interests during the Cold War and the war in Afghanistan may have led successive administrations to be less critical of Pakistan's civil-military establishment.

“And there's certainly an opportunity for the United States to do more,” he added.

On India-U.S. relations, Mr. Blinken described the transformation in ties over the past few decades as a shift from estrangement to a strategic partnership, underpinned by shared interests and people-to-people connections.

articles.title: China border has become 'more alive,' India enhancing frontier infrastructure: Jaishankar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The External Affairs Minister said India's capability to "deploy" its troops on that border has seen "a very marked" improvement

India's border with China has become "more alive" and requires a much greater commitment of Indian troops on a sustained basis, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) as he listed New Delhi's policy approach to enhance infrastructure along the frontier.
Mr. Jaishankar also said that India has bolstered its military capabilities along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) since the deadly clashes in Eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley in 2020.

His remarks at an interactive session at the HT Leadership Summit came amid ongoing efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to normalise their relations that came under severe strain following the over four-year border face-off in Eastern Ladakh.

"Just think about the last few years. How often do you now read - a new tunnel has been built, some new bridge has been built, another airfield has been commissioned. You're getting this news with greater and greater frequency," he said.
"What has happened today is the border with China has become more alive in a way. It has required a much greater commitment of troops on a sustained basis."
"The fact is that the work we had already done allowed that kind of numbers to be deployed out there, and the work we continue to do will maintain those numbers," he said.

After over four years of frosty ties over the eastern Ladakh military standoff, India and China began to repair relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping in the Russian city of Kazan in October 2024 that took place after the face-off ended.
The talks between Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi covered a range of issues, including reducing their trade deficit, tackling challenges like terrorism and ensuring fair trade in multilateral platforms.

"I would say when it comes to the border, I would honestly make this point, and I think there's a lot of data and evidence to back it up, which is that the border infrastructure was really neglected till about a decade ago. I mean, people spoke about it, people drew up plan," Mr. Jaishankar said.

"If you actually go on the ground and see year-by-year how many kilometres of roads, what was the tunnelling, what was the positioning, I think anybody, and certainly anybody associated with the armed forces dealing with that sector knows the truth," he noted.

articles.title: U.S. air travel should recover from ground stop by end of November 15, FAA says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: New technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated equipment and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the flight shutdown of more than four hours, Trump administration officials said
U.S. air travel should be fully recovered from the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years by the end of Sunday, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
Mr. Bedford said the flights “will still have delays and cancellations” on Saturday (November 14) but promised that the “worst is behind us.”

New technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated equipment and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the flight shutdown of more than four hours, Trump administration officials said.

Planes were taking flight and landing on Saturday (November 14), Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said. But the effects could be felt for days. Officials say the system will likely return to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.

The nationwide stop was the first since January 2023, when another key Federal Aviation Administration computer system that sends notices to pilots malfunctioned, and the second since the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Andrew Charlton, an aviation consultant, said Friday's (November 13) stoppage affected about a quarter of the 45,000 flights in the U.S. each day.

“The knock-on effect of that is incredible,” said Mr. Charlton, managing director of Aviation Advocacy. “The aircraft doesn't just fly from A to B and back to B and then stop. It then moves onto C and then over to E and around and around and around. It is, of course, exacerbated if you're talking about long-haul flights, international flights over the Atlantic or over the Pacific.”
At airports, passengers stared at screens showing delays or rushed to find buses or trains to their destinations.

Emily Brown and her 14-year-old daughter waited more than four hours on Friday (November 13) at the Dallas airport for their flight to Columbus, Ohio, before giving up. They were travelling to surprise her daughter's best friend. Instead, she had to settle for phoning the friend through tears in the airport, Ms. Brown said.
“She saved up her money to buy her own ticket, and she's planned this whole weekend,” Ms. Brown said. “Now we're not sure when we're gonna be able to go.”

Andrew Charlton, an aviation consultant, said Friday's (November 13) stoppage affected about a quarter of the 45,000 flights in the U.S. each day.

“The knock-on effect of that is incredible,” said Mr. Charlton, managing director of Aviation Advocacy. “The aircraft doesn't just fly from A to B and back to B and then stop. It then moves onto C and then over to E and around and around and around. It is, of course, exacerbated if you're talking about long-haul flights, international flights over the Atlantic or over the Pacific.”

At airports, passengers stared at screens showing delays or rushed to find buses or trains to their destinations.

Emily Brown and her 14-year-old daughter waited more than four hours on Friday (November 13) at the Dallas airport for their flight to Columbus, Ohio, before giving up. They were travelling to surprise her daughter's best friend. Instead, she had to settle for phoning the friend through tears in the airport, Ms. Brown said.

“She saved up her money to buy her own ticket, and she's planned this whole weekend,” Ms. Brown said. “Now we're not sure when we're gonna be able to go.”

articles.title: Benjamin Netanyahu calls for Israeli unity government, Eisenkot dismisses ‘tricks’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The latest exchange comes as Mr,. Eisenkot is in the midst of negotiations to form a government, after he was tapped for the post of premier on Nov. 15, 2026

Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday (November 14, 2026) reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot , who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse.
The latest exchange comes as Mr,. Eisenkot is in the midst of negotiations to form a government, after he was tapped for the post of premier on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

A meeting with Mr. Eisenkot on Thursday (November 13, 2026) “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Mr. Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”.

Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc vote in favour of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers. The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset, which has 120 seats.

“Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let’s meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts, and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state,” Mr Netanyahu urged.
Minutes later, Mr. Eisenkot responded by saying Mr. Netanyahu “knows he lost the election”, accusing him of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government.

“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow,” the former army chief said, adding that “these tricks don’t work on me”.

articles.title: Congress wants to contest 181 seats in 2027 UP polls, indicates Akhilesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Asked if the demand was of 200 seats, he replied, "A little less than that." When the interviewer suggested 180 seats, Mr. Yadav said, "Add one more," indicating that the Congress has sought 181 seats from the SP

Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav indicated on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that the Congress has expressed its wish to contest 181 seats in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, while asserting that the INDIA bloc would remain united to defeat the ruling BJP in the State.

Asked at summit in Delhi whether the Congress is seeking to contest 100 seats, Mr. Yadav said the party has demanded more than that. Asked if the demand was of 200 seats, he replied, "A little less than that." When the interviewer suggested 180 seats, Mr. Yadav said, "Add one more," indicating that the Congress has sought 181 seats from the SP.

"We have made up our mind on how many seats we will contest. The Samajwadi Party and the INDIA alliance will defeat the BJP together," he said, adding that the "theft" of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya will be a major poll issue.
Asked if he is considering an alliance with Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati, Mr. Yadav said he does not think of other alliances while being part of an existing one.
He said the SP has a good experience of forging alliances and has brought together people who believe in the principles of B R Ambedkar.
"The INDIA alliance with the Congress is the same alliance that we had earlier. I do not see any change in it," the former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister said.
On his proposed visit to the Ram temple, Mr. Yadav said he would first visit the Kedareshwar Dham in Etawah and then seek the blessings of Lord Ram.
He said SP leaders have arranged an invitation for him after consulting prominent people and fixing an auspicious date.
A senior SP leader had earlier claimed that Yadav will visit Ayodhya on December 12.
"I will have darshan first and then seek blessings," Mr. Yadav said.

Asked if he is considering an alliance with Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati, Mr. Yadav said he does not think of other alliances while being part of an existing one.

He said the SP has a good experience of forging alliances and has brought together people who believe in the principles of B R Ambedkar.

"The INDIA alliance with the Congress is the same alliance that we had earlier. I do not see any change in it," the former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister said.

On his proposed visit to the Ram temple, Mr. Yadav said he would first visit the Kedareshwar Dham in Etawah and then seek the blessings of Lord Ram.

He said SP leaders have arranged an invitation for him after consulting prominent people and fixing an auspicious date.

A senior SP leader had earlier claimed that Yadav will visit Ayodhya on December 12.

articles.title: India votes against UNGA resolution calling for global moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India has voted against a draft UN General Assembly resolution calling on nations to establish a moratorium on the death penalty.

The 193-member UNGA adopted, by recorded vote, the resolution on Friday (November 13, 2026) introduced by Mexico on ‘Moratorium on the use of the death penalty’, with 133 countries voting in favour of the resolution, 33 against and 16 abstentions.
India, along with Bahrain, China, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Japan, Kuwait, Maldives, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the U.S., voted against the resolution.

The resolution expressed deep concern about the continued application of the death penalty and reaffirmed the right of all countries to develop their own legal systems, including determining appropriate legal penalties in accordance with international law.

It called upon all States to establish a moratorium on executions, with a view to abolishing the death penalty. It also called upon States which have abolished the death penalty not to reintroduce it.
The resolution expressed deep concern that, despite the global trend towards limiting the application of the death penalty, there was a significant surge in reported executions in 2025.

The resolution called upon all States to progressively restrict the use of the death penalty and not to impose capital punishment for offences committed by persons below 18 years of age or whose age above 18 years at the time of the commission of the crime cannot be accurately determined.

It also called for restricting the use of the death penalty on pregnant women or on persons with mental or intellectual disabilities, as well as on older persons, and to reduce the number of offences for which the death penalty may be imposed, including by removing the mandatory application of the death penalty.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court asks security, police organisations to review mental health policies for armed personnel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order while quashing the criminal proceedings against a 37-year-old CISF Sub-Inspector for attempting to kill herself in 2022 by using her service pistol while on duty in Mangaluru

The High Court of Karnataka has advised the security and police organisations to prioritise the mental health and well-being of personnel entrusted with firearms while asking the authorities to examine existing policies and take appropriate steps to strengthen the mental health and welfare measures for their personnel.

Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order while quashing the criminal proceedings against a 37-year-old CISF Sub-Inspector for attempting to kill herself in 2022 by using her service pistol while on duty in Mangaluru. She had attempted to end her life following years of severe mental distress over her inability to conceive a child due to a blocked fallopian tube.

Allowing her petition, the court set aside the lower court’s order and discharged her from the offence under Section 309 of the IPC (attempt to commit suicide). The court ruled that Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, creates a mandatory presumption of severe stress, placing the burden on the prosecution to prove otherwise. Since no such evidence was produced, the court held that continuing the trial would be an abuse of the judicial process.

“Personnel serving in these forces are also human beings. They have families, relationships, responsibilities and personal problems. They experience grief, anxiety, financial difficulties, marital discord, illness in the family and other difficulties common to human life. Wearing a uniform or undergoing rigorous training does not make them immune to such problems,” the court said.

Further, the court said that “the expectation that they must remain available for duty at all times and discharge their responsibilities, come rain or shine, irrespective of their personal circumstances or mental condition, requires a change in institutional thinking.”

The concerned organisations must ensure that accessible and confidential counselling, professional mental healthcare and timely treatment are available to personnel at all levels, including those posted in remote and difficult locations, the court said.

Commanding and supervisory officers, the court emphasised, must be sensitised to recognise signs of distress and facilitate appropriate assistance, and personnel who undergo treatment or experience mental health difficulties must also receive suitable support for rehabilitation and return to duty, based on professional assessment.

“The welfare of personnel and the security of the public are not competing considerations. A force which looks after the mental and physical well-being of its personnel is better equipped to maintain discipline, operational readiness and public safety, the court said.

articles.title: Karnataka mandates gynaecological check-ups for girls, sex education in schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Child Protection Committees, CCTV cameras, counselling and awareness programmes among measures mandated by joint circular

The Karnataka government has recently issued a joint circular, with multiple concerned departments on board, on measures to ensure the well-being of students across all schools, colleges, hostels, residential schools, and training institutions in the State.

These measures include conducting mandatory check-ups for all girls in schools by a gynaecologist, the provision of sex education, and the creation of awareness among children regarding child rights, issues concerning teenage pregnancies, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, child marriage, and the Child Helpline (1098). Furthermore, the installation of CCTV cameras has been made mandatory in all schools and colleges.

A warning has also been issued stating that failure to prevent — or negligence in addressing — cases of child marriage, teenage pregnancy, and incidents falling under the POCSO Act, 2012, will result in both legal action and disciplinary proceedings against the officials concerned.
The circular is a culmination of a series of measures initiated in June 2025 over concerns about rising cases of child marriage and teenage pregnancy in the State.

Among the measures prescribed is the formation of Child Protection Committees in educational institutions across the State. The committee, comprising parents, children, and teachers, must meet once every three months, and the proceedings of these meetings should be duly recorded, the circular noted.

Schools and residential schools must install complaint boxes and take measures to address the grievances of girl students. It has been mandated that experienced and qualified counsellors be appointed in schools and Pre-University (PU) colleges to address the mental health and other challenges faced by adolescent students. Teachers must persuade parents to re-enrol girls who have dropped out of school and ensure that they continue their education until the age of 18. They must also take measures to prevent school-going children from being subjected to child labour.

Children should be provided with appropriate education to help them understand and identify issues such as crimes against children, child labour, child trafficking, sexual abuse, and child marriage through both formal and informal educational curricula. They should also be taught to recognise any form of abuse, violence, discrimination, or exploitation directed against them, whether within educational institutions or elsewhere, the circular said.

“If a girl student in a school or residential school remains absent for more than three days without providing any notification, the principal must inform the gram panchayat and the child helpline (1098) in writing. The Health Department has stated that appropriate legal action must be taken against shops selling abortion pills without a doctor’s prescription, as well as against doctors and members of the public involved in unauthorised abortion activities,” the circular said.

Additionally, the guidelines emphasise the need to raise awareness among children about the dangers of substance abuse and drug addiction, alongside conducting regular screenings for such issues. They stipulate that such awareness should also be integrated into the school curriculum.

articles.title: India, Egypt look to strengthen trade, investment ties, Piyush Goyal says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing a community event organised by the Indian Community Association in Egypt in Cairo, Piyush Goyal said the bilateral trade between the countries stood at about $6.5 billion

India is looking to expand trade and investment opportunities in Egypt, widen market access for its goods and services, and encourage imports of Egyptian products and capital inflows into India to foster mutually beneficial economic cooperation, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goya l said.
Addressing a community event organised by the Indian Community Association in Egypt (ICAE) in Cairo, he said the bilateral trade between the countries stood at about $6.5 billion.
But for the size of the two economies, "I believe it's just a beginning; it cannot be our destination; the sky's the limit", he said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
India's exports to Egypt during 2025-26 amounted to $3.87 billion, and imports stood at $2.60 billion.

India's major exports to Egypt include meat and poultry products, petroleum products, organic chemicals, cotton and machinery, and its major imports include crude petroleum, fertilisers, cotton and mineral products.

"We are looking at investment opportunities in Egypt; we are looking at marketing our goods and services...we are looking at Egyptian products coming to India and investments coming to India in areas of Egypt's strength, because ultimately trade has to be two-way. It has to be a win-win between the two nations," Mr. Goyal said, adding that the two countries need to aim for high trade numbers.

articles.title: Cape Verde could elect first woman President since gaining independence in 1975
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes
Cape Verde could elect its first woman President on Sunday (November 15, 2026) as former Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is seeking a second term.
Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes.

Ms. Rosa, backed by the Opposition Movement for Democracy, is the first woman to run for President since independence from Portugal in 1975. Women have held senior cabinet posts, but Cape Verde has never had a female prime minister or president.

In Cape Verde's parliamentary system, the Prime Minister directs government policy and holds most executive authority. The president's role is largely symbolic, although the directly elected head of state can veto legislation.

The Atlantic island nation off West Africa, home to about half a million people, has a record of peaceful transfers of power and competitive elections in a region where that is rare. Nearly 77,000 Cape Verdeans abroad are registered to vote, almost a fifth of the total electorate.

Many voters feel distant from their leaders and want a president who understands their daily difficulties, while limited economic prospects were driving young people to seek opportunities abroad, said Roselma Evora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde.
Mr. Neves, who won in 2021 with about 52% of the vote, has pledged to build cross-party support to improve housing, healthcare and education, create jobs and raise wages.
Incumbency gives Mr. Neves greater visibility, including among overseas voters, Evora said.
Ms. Rosa's candidacy challenges traditional expectations of women's roles in a society that remains “very patriarchal,” Evora said.

Ms. Rosa has centred her campaign on maintaining a balance of power, arguing that the country needs a counterweight to the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde, which backs Neves and controls the government and most municipalities.

articles.title: NATO to skip a leaders' summit in Albania next year as high-level meetings are scaled back
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte played down the issue. “We are flexible with NATO summits,” he said

NATO is scaling back its high-level meetings and will not hold a leaders' summit in Albania next year as previously planned amid tension within the alliance over defence spending, Iran and the war in Ukraine.

Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that “there is not yet a common position on when the summit will happen, for sure not in 2027.” He said that “in 2028, if it will be a summit, it will be in Tirana,” Albania's capital.

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte played down the issue. “We are flexible with NATO summits,” he told The Associated Press in an interview. “We have summits when we need them,” he said, and will hold the next one “when a necessity is there.”
Until about a decade ago, NATO held summits every two years.
It's not just about gatherings between U.S. President Donald Trump and his counterparts.

NATO Defence Ministers usually meet in October, but no talks took place last month, and none are planned for October 2027. Foreign Ministers only have one scheduled meeting next year, instead of two, under what NATO describes as a “reorganization package.”

U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have each skipped a NATO meeting or left before talks ended since they came to office. Mr. Hegseth has used defence ministerial gatherings to berate or cajole European allies and Canada.
The planned summit in Albania highlights the alliance's challenges. Albania was appointed next year's host in 2025, but its name was removed from a July summit declaration.

Some allies believe that Albania is not spending enough on defence and they were reluctant to reward the country with NATO's big event. The government in Tirana is projected to spend 2.15% of its gross domestic product on defense this year.

NATO's target is for the 32 allies to spend 3.5% of GDP on core defense by 2035, and 1.5% on defense-related infrastructure. Albania is not the worst offender among the 32 member countries. Spain, Belgium and Slovenia are faring much worse.

articles.title: Sirens sound in Bahrain as Iran’s Guards claim drone attack
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Bahrain, ⁠home to ⁠the U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet, urged citizens and ​residents to ‌remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location, ‌its Interior Ministry ​said
Sirens sounded in Bahrain and authorities told residents to seek shelter on Sunday (November 15, 2026) as Iran’s Guards said they had attacked a military base in the Gulf nation.
Alarm sirens blared, according to an AFP journalist, while authorities posted several alerts on social media, instructing people to shelter, but did not specify the source of the threat.
The interior ministry in an X post urged “residents to remain calm, proceed to the nearest safe location, and follow news through official channels for the protection of public safety”.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said their forces carried out a drone attack on a U.S. radar system at a base in Bahrain, according to a statement carried by the Iranian state broadcaster on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

“The U.S. air defense radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force,” the Guards said in a statement posted by the state broadcaster on Telegram.

Bahrain, which hosts a major U.S. naval base, is one of several Gulf countries that have borne the brunt of Tehran’s wrath during the war started when the United States and Israel launched surprise attacks on Iran on February 28.

On Friday (November 13, 2026), Iran’s Revolutionary Guards had said their forces targeted a US early warning radar system in Bahrain, with the American military saying it shot down two Iranian drones targeting the Gulf island.

During eight months of war, Iran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and struck infrastructure including airports, seaports, energy facilities, landmarks and US assets across the region.

articles.title: COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies.

The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change.
However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support.
According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health.
The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days.

Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems.

fullParagraphs: The episode discusses the everyday realities of living with diabetes, experiences of older adults who have managed the condition over several years, and practical approaches to diabetes management, including diet, physical activity and blood glucose monitoring
The 59th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, marking World Diabetes Day, explores the everyday realities of living with diabetes and approaches to managing the condition over time.

Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, speaks to individuals living with diabetes, including older adults who share their experiences of managing the condition over several years. Their experiences offer perspectives on living with diabetes and the importance of sustained management.
The episode also features a discussion with Dr. V. Mohan, Chairman and Chief of Diabetology, Dr. Mohan’s Diabetes Specialities Centre, Chennai, on practical approaches to diabetes care.

The discussion looks at the role of dietary habits and food choices in diabetes management, the importance of regular physical activity and exercise, and blood glucose monitoring. It also examines how sustainable changes to everyday food and activity routines can support long-term management of the condition.

The episode discusses practical measures that people living with diabetes can incorporate into their daily lives, the importance of consistent approaches to care, and how genetic predisposition and environmental factors influence the development and management of diabetes. It also explores longevity and living well with diabetes over the years.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for new distance record
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star
NASA's Voyager 1 is about to become humanity's first object to reach one light-day from Earth as it pushes ever deeper into interstellar space.
That's a mind-blowing distance of more than 26 billion kilometres for the spacecraft launched 49 years ago.

When Voyager 1 reaches that remarkable milestone on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day.
NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star.
Project manager Suzanne Dodd sees Voyager 1 as Earth's ambassador hurtling between stars while providing a “sense of wonder” on the home front.
“It's a national treasure,” she told The Associated Press . “Really extraordinary.”

To celebrate this moment, NASA is urging people from all corners to grab their phone or a flashlight to create a wave of golden light after sunset on Tuesday (November 17), using Morse code to spell the letters V-G-R, Voyager's call sign, into the night sky.

Despite sporadic problems typical of old age, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 continue to send back science and engineering data as they zoom toward different points in space at 61,000 kph. Although launched two weeks before its sibling in 1977, Voyager 2 won't reach the one light-day mark until 2035.

Voyager 1 swept past Jupiter and Saturn to scientists' delight in 1979 and 1980, respectively, before exiting the solar system. It reached what NASA defines as interstellar space — the expansive region between star systems — in 2012. Voyager 2 visited those two planets plus Uranus and Neptune, also sending back stunning photos, before entering interstellar space in 2018.

Almost every day, the Voyagers beam back details about their never-before-explored environment: the strength and direction of the magnetic field as well as tidbits about the surrounding pressure, dust and galactic cosmic rays. They're a bit like weather satellites, according to Dodd, who's worked with the Voyagers since 1984.

fullParagraphs: An analysis by the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) found that Delhi’s average PM2.5 concentration in the week preceding Deepavali reached 236 micrograms per cubic metre, the highest in three years

With the Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 400 at some locations in Delhi, people whose work keeps them outdoors for long hours say they are experiencing breathing difficulties, persistent cough, headaches and burning eyes, often without adequate protection against pollution.
For traffic police personnel, domestic workers, roadside vendors, mechanics and gig workers, staying indoors is rarely an option.

Yogendra Kumar, a traffic inspector posted in outer north Delhi, said pollution-related health risks for traffic personnel persists throughout the year but increases significantly when air quality deteriorates.

“The impact on health is inevitable in the outskirts, as road dust also contributes to pollution alongside emissions. We have no safeguards apart from masks. Prolonged exposure causes breathing problems and a persistent cough,” he said.
Reena Chaudhary, a domestic worker in Palam Colony, said she began experiencing breathing difficulties on the night before Deepavali, with her symptoms worsening on the festival day.

“I leave home around 7 a.m. and return by 9 p.m. I began having headaches and burning eyes the day before Deepavali, particularly while passing through smoke-filled lanes between houses at night. On Deepavali, my condition worsened. I felt dizzy throughout the day, had a persistent cough and just wanted to lie down. But who would work if I did?” she said.

Ms. Chaudhary said she had to walk through smoke on Deepavali night with her d upatta wrapped around her face. Since then, she has been taking her daughter along in case she falls ill and is unable to work.
Ravi, a 21-year-old gig worker who attends college during the day, said he works through the night, picking up rides across the city to support his family.
“Even at night, I can see that the air is dense and heavy. At times, I have to stop near a green area, such as Vande Mataram Marg, just to be able to breathe,” he said.
Mukesh Yadav, an e-rickshaw driver in Palam, said road dust remains a problem throughout the year, apart from smoke from firecrackers and vehicular emissions.

articles.title: Telangana Women’s Commission issues notices to eight ART centres in illegal oocyte racket case
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Telangana State Women’s Commission (TGSCW) has initiated an inquiry into an alleged illegal oocyte donation racket in Hyderabad, issuing notices to eight Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) centres and egg banks over suspected irregularities in their donor records and procurement practices.

The Commission examined representatives of the eight institutions on Friday, November 13, after directing their managements to appear before it. However, TGSCW Chairperson Nerella Sharada expressed dissatisfaction after some centres sent staff members and other representatives instead of senior management, despite being specifically instructed to attend in person. The inquiry was subsequently adjourned after the institutions assured the Commission that their management would appear at the next hearing.

During Friday’s proceedings, the Commission scrutinised reports, records and details of egg donors submitted by the ART centres and egg banks. “Several irregularities and suspicious elements have emerged from the records examined so far,” said Ms. Sharada.

She also questioned claims made by the institutions that nearly 90% of their egg donors came from other States and donated their eggs voluntarily without receiving any remuneration or financial compensation. She said the claims raised several questions and warranted further investigation.

Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare, Sangeetha Satyanarayana, also attended the inquiry, during which Ms. Sharada sought details about the progress of the department’s investigation into the alleged illegal egg procurement practices. The discussions also covered shortcomings in the existing Assisted Reproductive Technology Act and its implementation, particularly the challenges in regulating and monitoring ART centres and egg banks.

Ms. Sharada said she would soon meet Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to inform them of the findings and discuss corrective measures, including possible legislative amendments to strengthen regulation of the sector.

Ms. Sharada further said that the Commission has also received information indicating the possible involvement of several other ART centres and egg banks in the alleged racket. It plans to issue notices to their management and summon them for questioning as part of the ongoing inquiry.

“The Commission will not tolerate illegal practices that compromise women’s health, dignity and rights. We will continue the investigation in coordination with the concerned government departments to identify those responsible and ensure appropriate legal action,” she added.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 15 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Telangana Women’s Commission issues notices to eight ART centres in illegal oocyte racket case

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The Telangana State Women’s Commission (TGSCW) has initiated an inquiry into an alleged illegal oocyte donation racket in Hyderabad, issuing notices to eight Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) centres and egg banks over suspected irregularities in their donor records and procurement practices.

The Commission examined representatives of the eight institutions on Friday, November 13, after directing their managements to appear before it. However, TGSCW Chairperson Nerella Sharada expressed dissatisfaction after some centres sent staff members and other representatives instead of senior management, despite being specifically instructed to attend in person. The inquiry was subsequently adjourned after the institutions assured the Commission that their management would appear at the next hearing.

During Friday’s proceedings, the Commission scrutinised reports, records and details of egg donors submitted by the ART centres and egg banks. “Several irregularities and suspicious elements have emerged from the records examined so far,” said Ms. Sharada.

She also questioned claims made by the institutions that nearly 90% of their egg donors came from other States and donated their eggs voluntarily without receiving any remuneration or financial compensation. She said the claims raised several questions and warranted further investigation.

Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare, Sangeetha Satyanarayana, also attended the inquiry, during which Ms. Sharada sought details about the progress of the department’s investigation into the alleged illegal egg procurement practices. The discussions also covered shortcomings in the existing Assisted Reproductive Technology Act and its implementation, particularly the challenges in regulating and monitoring ART centres and egg banks.

Ms. Sharada said she would soon meet Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to inform them of the findings and discuss corrective measures, including possible legislative amendments to strengthen regulation of the sector.

Ms. Sharada further said that the Commission has also received information indicating the possible involvement of several other ART centres and egg banks in the alleged racket. It plans to issue notices to their management and summon them for questioning as part of the ongoing inquiry.

“The Commission will not tolerate illegal practices that compromise women’s health, dignity and rights. We will continue the investigation in coordination with the concerned government departments to identify those responsible and ensure appropriate legal action,” she added.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to move towards Andhra coast by November 19, rainfall expected in Tamil Nadu, Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The cyclone is expected to bring rains to Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal

A depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the meteorological department said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

Cyclone Akvan is expected to cause rains in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said. The department announced that the cycline is expected to move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19.

The Regional Meteorological Centre issued a Nowcast alert at 1 p.m. in Tamilnadu, valid till 4 p.m. for light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over Cuddalore, Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai, Nagappattinam, Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Thiruvarur and Viluppuram districts and Karaikal and Puducherry.

According to the latest weather report, Saturday's (November 14) well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved northwestward, intensified into a depression and lay centred at 5:30 a.m. today. It is very likely to continue to move northwestward, intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on November, 16 and into a severe cyclonic storm on November 17.

The data further added that in addition to northern Tamil Nadu districts, moderate rain at isolated places is likely to occur over western ghat and southern districts of the State from Monday (November 16).

The Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved nearly northwards with the speed of 10 kmph during past 03 hours and lay centered at 0830 hours IST of today, the 15th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 9.3°N and Longitude 86.9°E, about 630 km east of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 690km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 840 km east-southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 1010 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1130 km south-southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal on 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal on 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast during subsequent 2 days.
According to the bulletin, during the last 24 hours ending at 8:30 a.m. on Sunday (November 15), rainfall occurred in several districts, including Chengalpattu, Chennai, Kancheepuram and Kanyakumari.

The IMD alerted that the cyclone will bring heavy rain to some districts of West Bengal from November 19 to 21. It will bring heavy rain to the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, the department said. A downpour is also likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 kmph in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely.
A nip in the air over South Bengal is likely to dissipate as day and night temperatures will rise by two to three degrees Celsius from November 18, it said.

articles.title: Thiruvambady Devaswom welcomes rejection of Crime Branch probe report on Thrissur Pooram disruption
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devaswom had sought a fresh probe; Secretary Girish Kumar alleges conspiracy behind disruptions

Thiruvambady Devaswom secretary K. Girish Kumar has welcomed the State government’s decision to reject the Crime Branch report on the disruption of Thrissur Pooram, alleging that the investigation had failed to examine the conspiracy behind the incidents.

He said the Devaswom had sought a reinvestigation, and its representatives had met the Home Minister to press for a fresh probe. “The media and everyone else know what happened to the Pooram,” he said.

Citing several incidents, including the closure of the exhibition pavilion and attempts to prevent the umbrellas for the Kudamattam ceremony from being brought to the venue, Mr. Girish Kumar alleged that there had been a conspiracy to disrupt the festival. Despite these incidents, the Thiruvambady Devaswom had been blamed, he said, adding that he was happy that the Home Minister had examined these aspects.

Welcoming the rejection of the report, he questioned the suggestion that the two Devaswams could have deliberately disrupted the festival, pointing out that they incurred substantial expenditure on police security arrangements for the Pooram.
“The report portrayed the innocent as guilty,” he said, criticising the findings.
Describing the investigation as a case of entrusting the key to the thief, he alleged that those responsible for disrupting the Pooram had themselves been entrusted with investigating the incident.

The government returned the Crime Branch investigation report on the Pooram disruption case, citing lack of clarity in its findings. The Home Minister has directed the State Police Chief to submit a fresh report.

Citing several incidents, including the closure of the exhibition pavilion and attempts to prevent the umbrellas for the Kudamattam ceremony from being brought to the venue, Mr. Girish Kumar alleged that there had been a conspiracy to disrupt the festival. Despite these incidents, the Thiruvambady Devaswom had been blamed, he said, adding that he was happy that the Home Minister had examined these aspects.

Welcoming the rejection of the report, he questioned the suggestion that the two Devaswams could have deliberately disrupted the festival, pointing out that they incurred substantial expenditure on police security arrangements for the Pooram.

“The report portrayed the innocent as guilty,” he said, criticising the findings.

Describing the investigation as a case of entrusting the key to the thief, he alleged that those responsible for disrupting the Pooram had themselves been entrusted with investigating the incident.

The government returned the Crime Branch investigation report on the Pooram disruption case, citing lack of clarity in its findings. The Home Minister has directed the State Police Chief to submit a fresh report.

articles.title: Minorities have been underrepresented in Bengal Assembly
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Despite its reputation as a progressive State, women and Muslims have sparsely held power in West Bengal

The election process in West Bengal is approaching fast, amid an ocean of uncertainty over who will ultimately be able to cast their votes. In its final list, the Election Commission (EC) has placed nearly 60 lakh citizens under adjudication. While a supplementary list has been published, the fate of 27 lakh voters remains uncertain. The entire SIR exercise has created mayhem both in the administration and among citizens, and has pushed the issue of human development and social justice to the margins.

As most political parties have announced their candidates, it is worthwhile to assess their social group and gender composition. These candidate lists offer an important lens to assess the extent of commitment towards India’s pluralistic social fabric. However, what about the present composition of the State’s legislature? By conducting a critical assessment of the composition of the 17th West Bengal Legislative Assembly, one aims to evaluate the representation of various social groups in the State’s highest policymaking body. As State governments bear the bulk of the responsibility for designing, adjusting and implementing welfare policies effectively, the composition of the Assembly is crucial. Having representatives from various social groups makes sure that policy priorities address the needs of everyone in society.

articles.title: TMC government considered only Muslims as minority: Bengal CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “Minority does not mean a particular community. Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains are also [religious] minorities. The previous TMC government considered only Muslims as a minority,” says West Bengal CM

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 15, 2026) alleged that the previous TMC government had considered only Muslims as a minority, asserting that Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains are also religious minorities.
He visited the Gurdwara Bara Sikh Sangat at the city's trading hub, Burrabazar, and participated in a procession of the Sikh community in the area.

"Minority does not mean a particular community. Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains are also [religious] minorities. The previous TMC government considered only Muslims as a minority," the Chief Minister told reporters after greeting the members of the Sikh community in the gurdwara.
"They [Sikhs] are the truest patriots," the Chief Minister said.
Earlier, Mr. Adhikari had repeatedly accused the Mamata Banerjee -led government of indulging in the appeasement of the Muslim community to garner their support in the elections.

articles.title: Deep Ocean Mission important for India’s future: MoES secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is not done in the coastal area, but in the central Indian Ocean basin at water depths of about 5,000 metres. That’s very far from the coast., almost 2,500 km away, said Srinivasa Kumar Tumalla, MoES Secretary

Srinivasa Kumar Tumalla, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), has underscored the importance of the Deep Ocean Mission for India’s future, while seeking to allay concerns of coastal communities regarding potential impacts of deep-sea mining for seabed minerals on fishing and livelihoods.

Only exploratory surveys are progressing at the moment and that too, at a vast distance from the Indian coast, the MOeS Secretary told The Hindu on Friday on the sidelines of the 92nd annual meeting of the Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc) held at the National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS).

“This is not done in the coastal area, but in the central Indian Ocean basin at water depths of about 5,000 metres. That’s very far from the coast., almost 2,500 km away. Fishers need not be worried about that kind of impact,” he said.

At the same time, the Deep Ocean Mission, of which deep-sea mining for minerals is one component, holds critical significance for the country, the reason why the Union government has taken it up on mission mode, he said. Dr. Tummala emphasised the importance of developing technologies for tapping deep-sea mineral resources.

As per information given in the Parliament by the Centre in December 2025, India has ongoing exploration contracts with the International Seabed Authority (ISA) for polymetallic nodules (PMN) and polymetallic sulphides. Polymetallic nodules present in the seafloor contain metals such as nickel, copper, cobalt and manganese. Polymetallic sulphides contain copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver, gold and platinum among others. These metals are important for a host of technologies including electric vehicles and power grids. ISA is an autonomous entity established under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

Dr. Tumalla pointed out that actual mining operations would take time as the mining code has to become operational, and other procedures including comprehensive assessments of environmental impacts are completed. “Right now what is being done is only exploratory activities,” he said. India has contracts with ISA for about 75,000 sq km area in the central Indian Ocean basin for exploration of polymetallic nodules. The country also has about 10,000 sq km contracted for the search of polymetallic sulphides.

articles.title: Mahanagar Gas hikes CNG prices in Mumbai by ₹1.5/kg, sixth hike since May
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14
Amid rising costs of input gas, Mahanagar Gas Ltd (MGL) increased prices of compressed natural gas (CNG) at their retail outlets ₹1.5 per kg.
Effective November 15, CNG in Mumbai would be priced at ₹91.5 per kg in Mumbai.
Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14.
Moreover, the latest is the second hike in the ongoing month.

The uncertainty in West Asia and the loss of supplies from Qatar, which is the world’s largest LNG producer and among the most reliable suppliers, have obligated purchasers to further alternate scouting of the natural gas and increasingly buy at spot.

In a statement, MGL said, “The ongoing Middle East crisis, coupled with reduced domestic gas allocation and increased dependence on higher-cost imported RLNG linked to international benchmarks, has significantly increased MGL’s gas procurement costs, particularly for the CNG segment, driven by strong demand and a higher share of imported gas in its input mix.”
Previously, privately-owned Adani Total Gas too have also hiked CNG prices at their outlets cumulatively by ₹6.75 per kg across two tranches since October 23.

articles.title: Trump administration blames ‘overloaded’ systems for ground stop after FAA lets flights resume
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast

Trump administration officials said Friday (November 13, 2026) that new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated systems and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.
It was lifted Friday (November 13, 2026) night after a five-hour stretch when most flights were not allowed to take off from airports in the United States.

Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights were safely landed. But Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said he could not guarantee it wouldn't happen again.
Mr. Mullin said the FAA was installing “new equipment, new technology” and “it was overwhelming the older system.” There appeared to be no indication of a cyberattack, Mr. Mullin said.

A limited number of domestic flights began departing Friday (November 13, 2026) evening after the ground stop was lifted, but it would likely take days for airlines to fully recover because so many planes and crews were out of position. Officials said they think the system will be back to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.
The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Asked whether he could rule out a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence incident, Mr. Mullin said: “There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way.” He said there are no “footprints” showing an attack and that it appears to be “mechanically driven,” adding that officials were still looking for the cause.

At least 827 flights had been diverted. As of 7.05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

The airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted included Washington Dulles International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport and Nashville International Airport.
Some 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to take off from airports in the U.S. after 4 p.m. EST.

articles.title: Indian student jailed for 30 years for online child sex abuse in U.K.

fullParagraphs: The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15

A 27-year-old Indian student described by U.K. authorities as a “serial online groomer” was sentenced to 30 years’ imprisonment in north-west England on Friday (November 13, 2026) for “exploiting and coercing” several children online to commit sexual acts.

Bilal Kazi was sentenced at Chester Crown Court after pleading guilty to a series of child sexual abuse offences committed online. The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15.

“Bilal Kazi acted with absolute ruthlessness in grooming, manipulating and exploiting a large number of young vulnerable girls," said Martin McRobb, Specialist Prosecutor at the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

“He befriended them online and forced them to take photos and videos of them carrying out sexual acts. He then blackmailed those who refused to comply with his further demands, threatening to post the explicit imagery to others.

“He posed as a teenage boy in order to attract and gain the trust of his victims and caused many to think that they were in a genuine relationship with him. When the victims realised they had been deceived, they were understandably distressed, and some suffered serious and long-term trauma," he said.
The CPS said its Organised Child Sexual Abuse Unit presented the court with overwhelming evidence gathered by police investigators in Cheshire and the West Midlands.

“The scale of Kazi’s offending meant this was a truly mammoth investigation, requiring significant resources and close collaboration across the force,” said Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of the Online Child Abuse Investigation Team at Cheshire Constabulary.

“The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable. For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship. Exploiting that trust, Kazi manipulated them into believing that his behaviour was normal.

“His offending has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims. Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years. What should have been important formative years have instead been overshadowed by the trauma of Kazi's abuse," he said.

According to the police force, the first victim explained that she began speaking to Kazi on Snapchat when she was 13, believing him to be the same age. Their conversations quickly turned explicit in nature, with Kazi asking the victim several inappropriate questions.

articles.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the “chopstick arms” at SpaceX’s Starbase launch pad in Texas, in a milestone for fully reusable rockets

Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday (November 14, 2026) pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat showing the feasibility of fully reusable rockets that would bring affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality.

The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2.

The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems, a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible.

“That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds outside Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with the 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream.

“I really do believe this is the dawn of the space age,” said Dane Walter, 38, a spectator who came from Corpus Christi, Texas. “And truly, I consider it an equivalent moment to the Wright brothers at Kitty Hawk.”

It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. Until now, spaceships have been single-use items, discarded or destroyed after missions, making each launch an expensive, resource-intensive venture.
The Starship spacecraft orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Mr. Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey.

SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex, because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters. “I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!”

Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he said.

Analyst Kathleen Curlee, of Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology, hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done. “What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability is ready to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” she said.

articles.title: Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred
People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found.

Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age.
Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said.

"Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy.

Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes.

"While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said.

"Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.

articles.title: 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure.

These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others.

The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution.

Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas.

Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said.

In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)."
Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16.

Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function.

Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."
